exam_question: How electricity is generated in a hydroelectric power station
text:
The graph below demonstrates the cyclic process of electricity generation in hydroelectric power station.
Overall, there are two main steps consisted of pumping water and generating it to electricity. Moreover, it is clear that the flow of water goes forward and returns constantly.
At the beginning, the river flows down to the high level reservoir, which is mostly blocked by huge dam, and there is solely channel on the bottom intake water during the daylight hours. From the intake hole, water continues migrate to the generator located in the power station, where reversible turbines are operated. At this stage, two processes occur at the same time: while water goes to low-level reservoir, the electricity moves from the generator up to power lines and then to national grid.
The operation does not stop and on-going at night. The amount of water returns from the low point to the generator section, where it pumps by turbines into high-level reservoir and remain there, because intake section normally closed at night.

exam_question: The diagram below gives information about stages of the process of producing of olive oil.
text:
The diagram provides a detailed overview of the production process of olive oil, outlining the various stages involved.
Overall, the olive oil production process consists of seven distinct steps, commencing with the picking of olives from trees and culminating in the storage and selling of the final product in stores.
The initial stage of the process involves the manual harvesting of olives from trees, followed by the thorough rinsing of the olives with cold water to remove any impurities. Subsequently, the cleaned olives are subjected to a crushing process using a specialized machine to extract the olive paste from the fruit. Each step in this initial stage contributes to the preparation of the raw materials for oil production.
Moving on to the next phase, the olive paste is placed in bags with perforations to aid in the extraction of the oil. The extraction process involves pressing the paste using a large container, resulting in the separation of oil and olive stones. Finally, the extracted oil goes through a separation process to isolate it from the water, and is then stored and sold in stores for consumption.

exam_question: The diagram below shiws how tomato ketchup is made. Summarize the informatsion bu selecting and reporting the mani features.
text:
The diagram illustrates how tomato ketchup is manufactured.
Overall, for ketchup to be consumed, there are various stages, including harvesting, processing, and distribution.
The process begins on the farm, where tomatoes are hand-picked by farmers and put into baskets. Then, the farmers sort the tomatoes into good and bad ones. Once the tomatoes are sorted, a truck transports them to the factory. In the factory, the tomatoes go through the process of cleaning: they are peeled, and the stalks and seeds are removed. After they are cleaned, the tomatoes are placed into a container and crushed to get tomato juice, in which sugar, vinegar, and salt are added to create the ketchup flavor. After this, the mixture is boiled. Before pouring the mixture into the ketchup bottles, the mixture is left to cool down for two hours.
During the next several stages, the ketchup reaches the consumers. After being labeled, the bottles should pass quality control. It is after all these procedures that the bottles of ketchup are packed and distributed across supermarkets, where people may enjoy them with hamburgers and fries.

exam_question: The bar chart below shows the average rainfall for Australia by month for last year. The line shows the average rainfall for Australia by month for the last 40 years.Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:

Overall, the average rainfall for Australia last year was slightly lower than the forty-year average but followed a generally similar pattern, with fluctuations throughout the year.

Towards the end of the year, rainfall gradually increased again. The rainfall data for last year exhibited a comparable trend, with minor deviations.
While the general patterns are similar, there are some noticeable differences. The forty-year average begins at approximately 80 millimetres in January, dropping sharply to around 30 millimetres in April. It then decreases gradually to its lowest point, approximately 13 millimetres, in September before rising steadily to nearly 60 millimetres in December. Last year’s average rainfall was slightly lower than the forty-year average in most months. However, rainfall in March, May, June, and November exceeded the long-term average.
The most significant deviations occurred in August and October, when last year’s rainfall was particularly dry at around 5 millimetres each, compared to approximately 15 and 20 millimetres respectively for the forty-year average. These outliers highlight some irregularities in rainfall patterns for last year despite the overall alignment with historical trends.

exam_question: The graph below compares the changes in the birth rate of China and the USA between 1920 and 2000.
text:
The line graph illustrates changes in birth rates in China and the USA over an 80-year period, from 1920 to 2000. Overall, both countries experienced considerable fluctuations in their birth rates during the early part of the century, followed by a steady decline from the 1950s onwards.
Overall, while the birth rates of both China and the USA demonstrated periods of fluctuation, a general downward trend was observed in both countries. The USA maintained a higher birth rate than China for most of the period, although both nations saw their birth rates converge towards lower levels by the end of the century.
From 1920 to 1945, the birth rates in both countries followed a fluctuating pattern. The USA’s birth rate started at around 11 births per 1,000 people in 1920, slightly higher than China’s rate of approximately 10 per 1,000. Both countries experienced some fluctuations in birth rates during this period, although the USA’s birth rate remained consistently above that of China. Notably, there was a sharp decline in China’s birth rate around 1940, dropping from approximately 15 to almost zero.
Following this period, both countries witnessed a significant surge in birth rates between 1945 and 1950, known as the post-World War II baby boom. In China, this increase was especially dramatic, with the birth rate peaking at over 20 births per 1,000 people around 1950. The USA’s birth rate also rose during this period, reaching nearly 15 births per 1,000. However, after this peak, both countries began to see a gradual decrease in birth rates.
From the 1950s onwards, both nations experienced a consistent decline in birth rates. In China, the birth rate fell sharply, dropping below 10 births per 1,000 by 1970, and continued to decline steadily, reaching around 2 per 1,000 by 2000. Meanwhile, the USA’s birth rate decreased more gradually, stabilizing at around 7 births per 1,000 by the end of the period. Although the USA’s birth rate remained higher than China’s throughout the second half of the century, both countries had low birth rates by 2000

exam_question: The diagram below shows how a biofuel called ethanol is produced. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The given diagram illustrates the process of producing a biofuel named ethanol. Overall, there are seven main steps in the ethanol manufacturing process, beginning with the phenomenon that plants and trees use biological supplements to grow and ending with vehicles that consume ethanol and then release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
At the first stage of the diagram, sunlight and carbon dioxide are absorbed by vegetation to develop what is called photosynthesis. Once they have been harvested, the collected products undergo a pre-processing process that cuts them into strands of cellulose.
In the next step, the cellulose strands are transferred to a laboratory for processing to manufacture sugars, which are then combined with microbes to convert them into ethanol. This ethanol is then used as a fuel to power transportation with combustion engines, such as planes, trucks, or private cars. These vehicles will burn up the ethanol and release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. To reiterate this process, the emissions continue to circulate in the air, and the trees and plants, in turn, consume this as their food, and the cycle restarts.

exam_question: The diagram below shows how geothermal energy is used to produce electricity. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The diagram illustrates how geothermal power can be utilized to produce electricity.
Overall, this electricity production using geothermal energy is a linear process that starts with cold water pumped down through a well and ends with a generator producing the electricity, which is then sent to the electricity grid.
First of all, cold water is pumped down 4,5 km underground through the injection well. Then, the water passes through the geothermal zone, which has hot rocks to raise the temperature of the water. Once the water is hot, it is then pumped up through the production well to a condenser.
The last two steps are done above the ground, where the condenser turns the hot water into steam. The steam produced by the condenser is used to spin the turbines. Afterwards, the spinning turbines power the generator used to produce electricity. Finally, the electricity is transferred into the electricity grid through the power lines.

exam_question: The diagram below shows one method of manufacturing ceramic pots.
text:
The provided diagram illustrates a method utilized in the manufacture of ceramic pots.
The manufacturing process of ceramic pots, as depicted, comprises a series of 11 steps which involve the extraction of raw materials followed by various stages of processing and heating.
Initially, raw materials used in the production of ceramic pots are unearthed using a digging machine and then transported to a factory via a truck. Subsequently, at the factory, these materials are crushed into a fine powder. The powder is then mixed with water and poured into moulds to shape it into a pot. After molding, the pots are dried for a period ranging from 4 to 6 hours to create assembled clay pots.
Following the drying process, the clay pots undergo heating in an oven at a scorching temperature of 1000 degrees Celsius. Once heated, the pots undergo coloring and are fired in a different oven. This coloring and firing process gives rise to the final products, which are the completed ceramic pots.

exam_question: The diagram below shows the life cycle of the Monarch butterfly. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant
text:
The diagram illustrates the reproduction and transformation of the Monarch butterfly. The process is cyclical, comprising of four main stages from egg to adult.
Monarch butterflies lay their eggs on milkweed plants, and after approximately two weeks, the butterfly larva hatches. The larva subsequently develops into a caterpillar by itself, feeding on the milkweed as it grows. Once the caterpillar has reached a certain size, it attaches itself to part of the plant and hangs down, before covering its body in a type of temporary shell called a chrysalis. This contains the larva while the 10-day transformation into a butterfly takes place.
This pupal stage lasts until the fully-formed adult butterfly leaves the chrysalis. Following its emergence, the butterfly is now capable of flight and so it migrates south, where it remains for a six-month period. Upon returning north, the adult finds a partner and begins the mating process. When it is ready to lay its eggs, it finds a suitable milkweed plant and the whole process begins again.
Overall, the butterfly undergoes dramatic metamorphosis, before embarking on an epic journey.

exam_question: The diagram below shows the manufacturing process for making sugar from sugar cane. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The diagram illustrates the process of producing sugar from sugar cane, detailing seven key stages from cultivation to the final product.
The first stage involves growing sugar cane, which takes between 12 to 18 months to mature. Once the cane is fully grown, it is harvested either manually or with machinery. The harvested sugar cane is then transported to a facility where it undergoes crushing. In this stage, the cane is crushed to extract juice.
After extraction, the juice is purified using a limestone filter to remove impurities. The purified juice is then heated in an evaporator, boiling until it thickens into a syrup. This syrup is later transferred to a centrifuge that spins at high speeds to separate the sugar crystals from the syrup.
The final stage entails drying and cooling the separated sugar crystals, resulting in the production of raw sugar ready for packaging and distribution.
In summary, the process of making sugar from sugar cane is a systematic procedure involving cultivation, harvesting, crushing, purifying, evaporating, centrifuging, and finally drying and cooling. Each stage is crucial in transforming the raw sugar cane into consumable sugar by ensuring impurities are removed and sugar crystals are separated from the syrup.

exam_question: The plans below show the site of an airport now and how it will look after redevelopment next year. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The provided plans delineate the current configuration of Southwest Airport and the proposed enhancements scheduled for implementation in the upcoming year.
Significant modifications are slated to occur across the airport, with notable improvements in both accessibility and passenger facilities, resulting in a more efficient and accommodating layout.
Presently, the airport features six distinct areas, namely check-in, café, gates, passport control, security control, and transport control. Access to the airport is unidirectional; passengers enter through the departures corridor, which houses both the check-in area and a café, while the arrivals side remains devoid of any amenities. Following security and passport checks, departing travelers proceed along a walkway to the gates, whereas incoming passengers exit via passport control areas. This layout potentially limits the overall passenger experience, as indicated by the absence of facilities on the arrivals side.
In the proposed redevelopment, the airport’s structure will expand to encompass 18 distinct areas, effectively increasing capacity and functionality. Importantly, two access points will be established—one for departures and another for arrivals. New amenities will be introduced, including a baggage drop-off for departing passengers, as well as a café, ATM, and car hire facilities designated for arrivals. The future layout, configured in a Y-shape, will feature additional gates, significantly enhancing operational efficiency on peak travel days. Furthermore, the introduction of a sky-train will facilitate expedited transportation for passengers, thereby improving overall accessibility within the airport.

exam_question: The diagram below shows the water cycle in both forested and urban areas. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The pictures depict the movement of water in forests and human settlements.
Each process is a cycle involving six stages, starting with transpiration and evaporation and ending with water runoff. However, there are differences between two processes in certain steps.
Both cycles initial when water is evaporated or transpired from the foliage in the form of vapour. After that, it forms clouds, which result in the precipitation. Although the rainfall remains the same in both types of areas, evaporation and transpiration in urban land are reduced because of lack of trees.
The processes continue as the raindrops permeate into the topsoil and the subsoil, making a baseflow which runs on the water table. These two stages occur more effectively in forests than in cities. Moreover, the land in urban areas is more likely to be eroded by the flow. Simultaneously, an amount of water creates a runoff on the ground, which increases and becomes more polluted in cities. Finally, water is heated into steams, which reinvents the cycles.

text:
The given diagram illustrates the use of geothermal energy for producing electricity. Overall, there are five main stages involved, proceeding from pumping cold water downwards and culminating in distribution of electricity to different towers.
Initially, the cold water is stored in a large tank. It is then pumped down at a depth of 4.5 kilometers and passed into the injection well. It is further passed to the geothermal zone, where hot rocks are present. From this zone, hot water is produced. After this, the hot water is pumped up through the production well.
Following this, the hot water goes to the condenser, where it is condensed to produce steam. Steam is passed to the turbine and gives power to the turbine to rotate it. Finally, there is a generator that is activated by the turbine to produce electricity and deliver it to different houses of individuals.

exam_question: The diagram shows the water cycle, which is the continuous movement of water on, above, and below the surface of the Earth. Summaries the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where revelant.
text:
The picture illustrates the process in which water moves from ocean to air and then to land through a natural process called the water cycle.
Overall, the cycle has four main stages. Water evaporates, forms clouds, returns back on earth’s surface, and eventually runs back into the oceans.
During the first three stages, Surface water evaporates due to the heat from the sun. Approximately 80% of this water vapor comes from the oceans, also known as saltwater. Next, this vapor is condensed in the sky and forms clouds, which may travel to different locations. At the third stage, water in clouds falls down on Earth as rain or snow (the phenomenon known as precipitation) and creates Lakes as well as snow caps on mountains.
Following precipitation, some of the water reaches the impervious layer of the ground, and some run on the surface. Eventually, this water finds its way back into the ocean to complete the cycle. However, just before entering the ocean, the surface runoff mixes with saltwater, which has already moved into land, and pushes it back into the ocean.

As waves enter the chamber, water levels rise and fall, pushing air upwards and downwards through turbines situated above the chamber. These turbines are connected to a generator that produces electricity as they spin.
The second diagram highlights two potential locations for installing wave energy machines: closer to shore and farther out at sea. Machines positioned closer to shore are associated with smaller waves and consequently generate less energy. However, they are cheaper to install and maintain. Conversely, machines located farther from the shore encounter larger waves, producing more energy but incurring higher installation and maintenance costs.
In summary, the wave energy machine converts wave motion into electrical energy through air pressure and turbine movement. The choice of installation location influences both the energy output and the associated costs, with a trade-off between proximity to shore and energy efficiency.

exam_question: The maps below show a town centre in 1990 and the same town centre today. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:

Overall, the town center has undergone significant changes, with a notable increase in pedestrian areas, the conversion of houses into apartment blocks to accommodate a growing population, and the replacement of small local shops with a large shopping mall.
In 1990, the northern side of the town center was home to several small retail shops, including newsagents, grocers, bakers, butchers, cafes, and a childcare center. Across Smith Street, there was a park, a library, and a town hall. Smith Street itself was open to vehicular traffic, with no dedicated pedestrian zones. Similarly, Oldfield Street and Green Street also lacked pedestrian paths.
Today, many of the small retail shops have been replaced by a large shopping mall, which now dominates the northern part of the town center. Vehicular access to Smith Street has been restricted, and two zebra zones have been introduced on Oldfield Street and Green Street to improve walkability. Furthermore, the houses that once occupied the southern side of the town center have been replaced by apartment blocks to accommodate the rising population. Meanwhile, the park, library, and town hall have remained largely unchanged.
In conclusion, the town center has evolved significantly over the past three decades, with an emphasis on modernizing the area to accommodate both commercial and residential growth. The increase in pedestrian spaces and the shift towards apartment living reflect the town’s response to changing social and economic needs.

In the first step, In order process paper, used paper is collected and transported with the help of big containers through conveyor belt. Than the used paper is than made unfiltered pulp after added into water chemicals, the pulp than must be filtered to water being removed. In the subsequent stage, the filtered paper is added to a huge container with water and soap to be further cleaned and removed contaminant, like ink, with the help of pumping air into container. After than, again water and various chemicals are added to pulp before the final stage and rolling. Finally, the recycled paper is rolled.

exam_question: This is an IELTS writing task 1 sample answer essay of a diagram/process showing how rainwater is collected and used for drinking water in an Australian town.

Initially, rain which falls on the rooftop is collected by gutters, and then all water is passed through a drain pipe. Then all drain pipes are connected to a main pipe. exam_question: How electricity is generated in a hydroelectric power station
text:
The diagram below illustrate how a hydroelectric power station produced electricity. Overall, water from river stored into the dam, then dam use its high level to flow water through turbines at high speed, generators connected with turbines generate electricity.
First of all in a hydroelectric dam, the source of water in dam is from a river. Water is reserved in the dam reservoir known as High-level reservoir because of its height. Beneath the dam, there are gates that open the flow of water in day time and close it in night. When gates are open in day, water flow from dam into the turbines that are at low level at high speed. This high speed of water produce because of height difference between dam and turbine make turbine wings to revolve at high speed.
At high spin of turbines, it run the generator connected to it. And this generator in the end generate electricity. that electricity move from power line into national grid to distribute. Extra water that already passes through turbines dumped into Low-level reservoir.

Overall, there are seven steps in the procedure of olive oil manufacturing, started with picking the olives from trees and ended up with storage and sale of the oil.
First of all, olives are picked and collected in containers, then they rinsed using cold water. After that, the clean olives are transferred in a belt to a machine to be smashed. In addition, smashed olives have two faiths as olive stones or as olive paste.
Second, further processing in the olive paste lead to olive oil production. Olive paste is collected in large bags with holes, which allow the liquid part to squeezed out. Then, the bags are pressed under weights to extract the liquid, after that, this liquid is separated into oil and water in a special tank. Finally, olive oil is stored and sold to the markets.

exam_question: The diagram below illustrate how recycled paper is made. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparison where relevant.
text:
The diagram illustrates the process for manufacturing recycled paper.
Overall, this is a mechanical process comprising four main stages: pulp creation, filtration, cleansing, and paper production.
The first stage starts with the collection of used paper, which is placed onto a conveyor belt. The paper is then transferred into a pulping machine, where it is mixed with water and chemicals to break it down into a slurry.
During the second stage, the pulpy mixture is sieved, which results in a more homogeneous and cleaner pulp. The third stage is the cleaning phase, where the pulp is thoroughly washed with water and soap. Additionally, the air is fed into the pulp so that smaller impurities, such as ink particles, can be removed. The pulp thereafter undergoes another round of chemical and water treatment.
Once the cleaning step has been completed, the pulp is laid out on a conveyor belt and passed through heated rollers, which press and dry the pulp into paper. The paper is subsequently rolled up, resulting in rolls of recycled paper ready for distribution and use.

exam_question: The diagram below shows a simple system that turns dirty water into clean water.
text:
The diagram illustrates a simple water filtration system that converts dirty water into clean drinking water.
The system consists of two main components: a cylindrical filter and a storage drum. The filter, which has a plastic lid, is divided into two sections. The top half holds the dirty water, while the bottom half contains three filtration layers: sand at the top, charcoal in the middle, and gravel at the bottom. Dirty water is poured into the filter and passes through these layers by gravity. The sand traps larger pollutants, the charcoal absorbs impurities and odors, and the gravel further purifies the water. Once filtered, the clean water flows through a pipe at the bottom of the filter into the storage drum, where it can be accessed via a faucet for drinking.
Compared to more complex filtration systems, this method is simple and cost-effective, though it may be less efficient for heavily contaminated water due to its reliance on basic materials.

exam_question: The diagram below shows how a biofuel called ethanol is produced. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The given pictures explains the production process of biofuel, which is called ethanol.
Overall, the process is cyclic and takes place in the industry. It consists of six main stages, beginning with using sunlight and carbon dioxide to generate power, which serve as the raw materials, and ending up with the production of ethanol.
In the first stage, energy is made from two resources, including sunlight and carbon dioxide and then, the plants and tree grow by energy consumption. In the following stage, the plants are harvested by special trunk and subjected to milling machine in the pre-processing phase to yield cellulose.
In the next step, cellulose is processed in the laboratory by utilizing some chemical compounds and sugars is generated. Subsequently, microbes are added to sugars and ethanol is produced. Finally, ethanol is consumed by transportation and carbon dioxide is generated again to be used as the raw material for biofuel substance generation.

exam_question: The diagram below shows how geothermal energy is used to produce electricity. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The diagram illustrates the process of electricity generation using geothermal energy in the geothermal power plant.
At the first stage of electricity generation, cold water is pumped down into the injection well, the depth of the well is 4.5km. Next, the cold water enters to the geothermal area consisted with hot rocks in order to heat the cold water into hot water. The hot water is then pumped up from the production well which is wider than the injection well and is the same length as it into the condenser.
When hot water is pumped up into the condenser, it will be condensed in order to convert it into steam and then the steam is sent to the turbine. The turbine can be powered by the steam to make it spin to trigger the generator. Finally, the generator is powered by the turbine and generate amounts of electricity.
We can see that it will need 6 steps to transform cold water into electric power and the generator is powered by water indirectly.

exam_question: The diagram below shows how rain water is collected and then treated to be used as drinking water in an Australian town. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant. You should write at least 150 words.
text:
The supplied diagram depicts the process of rainwater collection and purification procedure to make it drinkable, in the town of Australia. Overall, the rainwater harvesting process includes five major steps before the purified water reaches the consumer.
First of all, the rainwater is collected from individual houses, which rains on rooftops of houses, through interconnected drain pipes and is supplied to a water filter. Then, after filtration in a water filter chamber, the filtered water is stored in a large storage tank. Next, after enough water is stored in tank, the stored water is supplied to the water treatment tank. Here, water goes through different chemical treatments to make it drinkable.
The further steps include the distribution of treated water to individual houses. This is accomplished by means of interconnected supply pipe systems. In turn, this water is used for various household activities like drinking, washing, cleaning, gardening, and so on. This cycle continuous and is proven to be best method to purify rainwater.

exam_question: The diagram below shows the manufacturing process for making sugar from sugar cane. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The provided illustration outlines the sequential stages involved in the production of sugar from sugar canes.
Overall, the process encompasses the growth of sugar canes over a period of 12-18 months, the harvesting and extraction of juice, purification of the juice using a limestone filter, evaporation to form syrup, and the final separation of sugar crystals using a centrifuge, following which the juice undergoes drying and cooling.
The initial phase of the process involves the cultivation of sugar canes for approximately 12 to 18 months, and subsequently, they are harvested either through automated means or manually. The harvested canes undergo juicing using a specialized machine to extract the juice. The extraction process yields cane juice, which is then subjected to purification through a limestone filter to remove impurities.
Further in the process, the purified juice is transferred into an evaporator to remove excess water, transforming it into a syrup-like consistency. This syrup then undergoes separation in a centrifuge, resulting in the extraction of sugar crystals. The final steps involve the drying and cooling of the sugar, after which the finished sugar crystals are ready for packaging and distribution.

exam_question: The diagram below shows the manufacturing process for making sugar from sugar cane. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The diagram illustrates the process of producing sugar from sugar cane, which involves seven main stages, from planting the cane to the final product.
Firstly, sugar is derived from sugar cane, which takes between 12 to 18 months to grow. Once it is fully grown, farmers harvest the plant either by hand or using a tractor, with the second method being preferred due to its ability to harvest the plant on a larger scale. In the next stage, the sugar cane branches are crushed by a machine to extract the sugar juice. The juice is then purified using a limestone filter. After that, the juice is heated up in an evaporator to reduce its water content until the syrup is produced.
During the sixth stage of sugar production, the syrup is sent to a centrifuge machine. This machine separates the sugar crystals from the syrup. The sugar crystals are then dried and cooled to become sugar. exam_question: The diagram below shows the process for recycling plastic bottles. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The given diagram illustrates the recycling process of plastic waste, for example, bottles.
In general, the plastic bottle recycling took place in nine steps, starting with throwing the stuff into recycling bin, and successfully ends by converting the waste into useful products.
To begin with, after throwing the trash in the bin, it is further collected by the truck, which is the second step. In the next step, the waste collected is sent to the recycling centre for process of sorting. After segregation, the material is compressed, and then converted into blocks with the help of compressing machine. Then, crushing process takes place. The crushed stuff then undergoes next step, which is washing.
Subsequently, by using machine, the plastic pellets are produced, which are later heated to form raw material. Lastly, this raw material is used to improvise useful end products, and then delivered to the shops for the sale to the customer.

exam_question: The diagram below shows the process of making olive oil. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The diagram showcases the production of olive oil.
Overall, the oil manufacturing process can be divided into 3 parts. The first step is the collection and preparation of the necessary materials; the second is producing; and the last step is exporting to customers.
In the first process, olives are raked down and stored in vats for 2-3 days. After which, they are run through cool water, prepared to be pressed and turned to oil. In the second process, the olives are crushed by hammers in a machine. The olive stones are separated and contained in a container, while the remaining paste is then pressed and filtered in a hydraulic press. After which, the paste is fully turned into an oil substance.
In the last part of the olive oil production process, the freshly pressed and filtered oil is then put in a centrifuge to forcefully be separated into water and oil. The latter is then bottled and ready for distribution to customers.

Overall, the process involves collection, shredding, heating, melting, rolling, recycling, and reusing, processing materials in an environmentally friendly endless loop.
Firstly, cans are collected and sent to a smelting plant. Once they arrive, the cans undergo a cleaning and shredding process. Cleaning helps prevent bad smells and insects, and makes it easier for the recycling center to process them. Shredding crushes it into smaller pieces.

exam_question: The diagram below shows the water cycle in both forested and urban areas. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
text:
The water cycle plays a key role in maintaing a healthy ecosystem. Life would be impossible without rain! The diagrams showcase how various environmental factors both positively and negatively impact the rain cycle.
The picture on the left demonstrates the process of precipitation in a rainforest. The presence of trees and permeable topsoil encourages plenty of evaporation and transpiration, leading to a sufficient amount of clean rain. On the contrary, the absence of trees and construction of cemented roads in a developed city allow for minimal evaporation and transpiration. This naturally leads to fewer and shorter rain spells and extensive dry periods.
Moreover, the soft and porous soil in a forest lets most of the rainwater absorb into the ground, rasing the water table and expanding our underground water reserves. This in turn supports local vegetation, produces minimal runoff, and prevents erosion. On the other hand, the roads and pavements of a metropolitan city prevent rainwater from seeping into the ground. Instead, most of it turns into polluted runoff that flows into the nearest waterbody. Aditionally, the absence of trees coupled with high volume runoff cause increased erosion of healthy soil.
It is quite evident that trees play a massive role in determinig the quality of the water cycle. Thus, it is essential that we introduce more vegetation into our big beautiful cities.

exam_question: The diagram illustrates the process that is used to manufacture bricks for the building industry
text:
The brick manufacturing process is a systematic procedure comprising seven distinct stages that transform raw materials into finished products for the construction industry.
This comprehensive process begins with the extraction of clay and culminates in the delivery of packaged bricks, involving a series of critical steps that ensure quality and efficiency.
Initially, the process commences with the extraction of clay from beneath soil surfaces utilizing a digger. The extracted clay lumps are subsequently placed on a metal grid, where they are mechanically reduced into smaller particles. This clay is then combined with sand and water on the grid, ensuring a homogenous mixture through the use of a roller. The resulting mixture can either be shaped into bricks using a wire cutter or formed in dedicated molds, establishing the foundational shape of the bricks. Following this shaping phase, the newly formed bricks are transferred to a drying oven where they undergo desiccation for a duration ranging from 24 to 48 hours.
Upon completion of the drying process, the bricks are subjected to a two-phase firing method in a kiln. Initially, the bricks are exposed to moderate temperatures, between 200°C and 980°C, for approximately 48 to 72 hours. Subsequently, they are fired at elevated temperatures, reaching between 870°C and 1300°C, enhancing their strength and durability. After the firing is completed, a cooling phase occurs within a cooling chamber, lasting an additional 48 to 72 hours to ensure gradual temperature reduction. Ultimately, the finished bricks are meticulously packaged and prepared for delivery, often to construction sites or storage facilities, marking the conclusion of the manufacturing cycle.

exam_question: The diagram illustrates the process that is used to manufacture bricks for the building industry.
text:
The flow diagram illustrates the manufacturing process of bricks for the building business. Overall, the processes are separated into three main phases: raw material segregation, drying, and packaging.
The first phase mainly begins with the clay extraction by using excavator, then move the material to the roller that equipped with the metal grid to separate the required material with the residual. The next step in this phase in adding sand and water into the selected clay, then mix them into a mould to be formed as bricks.
Secondly, bricks will be cut based on the required size per batch. After that, bricks will be brought to the drying oven and later dried for around 24 to 48 hours to meet their standard. Later on, the bricks will be once dried in a higher temperature, from 200 to 980 Celsius degree for the moderate process, and from 870 to 1300 Celsius degree for the high one. The last step of this phase is cooling the bricks in the cooling chamber.
The last step is packaging process. After bricks exited the cooling chamber, they will be packed in one bulk. The bulk then moved to the container and then transported to their off-takers.

exam_question: **There are severe social consequences to housing shortages in cities and only the government can solve these problems.** **To what extent do you agree or disagree?**
text:
Some argue serious social matters arising from the shortage of housing in urban can be pragmatically remedied by the government. In my opinion, their viewpoints are legitimate because private sectors in this area remain low and the government should bear the burden of responsibility.

The most frequently cited rationale for the limited support from private enterprises is their profit-focused objective. This argument rests on the fact that most real estate and construction firms are driven to generate as much profit as possible and incline towards serving the wealthy. This can be most apparently seen in myriad luxury apartments in New York, which were built at the expense of government housing projects. These efforts have pushed the underprivileged citizenry out of their home, dragged them further from work, and engendered a wide breadth of social instability. The accumulated evidence has reasoned for the private companies' neglect towards social problems.

Albeit conceding that private businesses have no responsibility, I would contend that government intervention would play a pivotal role in containing these consequences to the scarcity of houses. This is predicated based on the assumption that governments can either build themselves using taxes or accept bids from construction companies. One of the salient illustrations of this is often indicated in undeveloped or poorly planned areas for new houses, which private housing developers can set foot in and bid with the government's supervision. These areas are predisposed to be unavailable for commercial exploitation and this gives governors more power over business moguls. Therefore, governments having the full responsibility to counter these issues in urban confers a valid standpoint as they can create new residential areas with affordable prices.

In conclusion, whilst private companies would not take the social side into account, governments are the catalyst for all housing solutions. In my final thought, governors and private city planners should jointly propose a more holistic approach in order to strike some balance in providing more convenient and affordable homes.

exam_question: Although families have influence on a children’s development, factors outside the home play a bigger part in their lives nowadays. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
Many today feel that the home no longer plays the largest role in child development. In my opinion, though outside factors have become increasingly invasive, family life is still more influential.

Those who believe children these days are largely shaped by the outside world often focus on the expanding importance of technology. Decades ago, it was more common for families to engage in conversation throughout the day, at dinner, and during holidays. Today, each family member might be more engaged with their smartphone, tablet, or laptop. For example, children now have constant access to streaming video sites like YouTube. Instead of watching cartoons for an hour a day on television, they can watch shows all day long, both in and outside the home. The result is that kids often find niche channels and parents have a difficult time monitoring and keeping up with the appropriacy of their interests and influences.

Nonetheless, family life remains the heart of early psychological development. Children are unlikely to have much access to new technology in their early years when researchers say the majority of personality formation occurs. If parents are strict, unforgiving and withhold their love then children begin to either turn inwards feeling rejected or strive compulsively for their parent’s esteem. These early, learned behaviours will manifest themselves in progressively more unhealthy behaviours and evolve as the child matures. Conversely, a child who is loved unconditionally but given honest feedback from their parents has a much greater chance of becoming a well-adjusted adult with strong role models to imitate.

In conclusion, despite the ubiquity of technology today, family is the key catalyst in early development. Regardless of changes in society, parents will continue to be the main influence for their children in the foreseeable future.

exam_question: 46.The manufacturing and use of cars damages the environment but their popularity is increasing. Why is this? How could this be controlled?
text:
Across the globe, the automobile industry is booming despite its adverse influences on the environment. In this essay, I will explore some reasons behind this phenomenon and recommend some solutions to control the situation.

To begin with, it is undeniable that cars continue to be manufactured because they are the most comfortable, popular and convenient means of transportation which are available to the most people. This is evident by the fact that there were about 1.5 billion vehicles worldwide in 2022. Furthermore, the automobile industry has made significant advancements in technology, making cars more appealing to customers. More specifically, the introduction of electric and hybrid cars has provided consumers with a more friendly environmental option although their availability and affordability are still limited compared to other traditional combustion engine models. In addition, the automobile sector is deeply integrated to the global economy, generating significant employment opportunities and contributing to economic growth. This creates an incentive for governments to support and promote this sector.

However, due to the detrimental effects on the habitat, it is imperative to control the manufacturing and use of car. Obviously, governments play an important role in this process. Firstly, they can enact and enforce strict emission standards for cars. They can also impose taxes for high-emission cars while offering incentives for electric or fuel-efficient ones. For example, the Canadian provincial and federal government introduced a program named "The Incentive for Zero-Emission Vehicles" and tax write-offs for businesses, to make these types of cars more affordable, encouraging its citizens to adopt clean technology. Thanks to this program, the market share of zero-emission vehicles hit a record of 10.5% in the second quarter of 2023. Secondly, authorities should increase their investment in public transportation, making it a sustainable and viable alternative. If governments can provide a more reliable and convenient mode of transport, they can encourage their residents to choose this option, reducing reliance on private cars.

In conclusion, the convenience of travelling by car and the economic significance of the automobile industry are two main factors contributing to the popularity of the manufacturing and use of cars in spite of the negative impacts on the environment. To mitigate this problem, governments can implement policies to encourage their residents to adopt fuel-efficient vehicles and engage in public transportation.

exam_question: In many countries, crime rates amongst younger people has been rising. Discuss the causes and solutions for this problem.
text:
In recent times, the rate of crime has been on the rise globally, especially the crime committed by young people. In this essay, I will shed some light on the factors contributing to this problem and will also suggest some solutions for the same.  

There are several reasons for the swell in criminal activity among the young people around the world. The first reason is the growing rate of divorce and the emergence of single parenthood. One good illustration of this is a study indicating that 50% of the convicted youth in the prisons of USA belong to a disrupted family. Secondly, it is also possible to say that the increasing drug abuse among many youths plays a significant role in the sudden increase in the incidents of crimes. Finally, although not a major cause but school dropout is also a contributing factor to increasing crime rates.  

However, solutions are available to tackle this problem. Firstly, governments and local authorities should work relentlessly to ensure that all youngsters are regularly attending their schools. In fact, a recent study in Washington, USA has concluded that students who managed to obtain their high school degree were 75 % less likely to engage in any criminal activity compared to those who could not complete their high school. Another possible solution is to invest more heavily in behavioral rehabilitation centers for youngsters convicted by law.   

Thus, criminal activity by young adults is a growing global problem, mainly caused by divorce, drug addiction and lack of education. These problems are not insurmountable, though, and governments should be able to solve these problems; they could start by considering the solutions suggested above.

exam_question: It is a natural process for animal species to become extinct (e.,g., Dinosaurs, dodos etc.). There is no reason why people should try to prevent this from happening. Do you agree or disagree?
text:
It is a natural process for animal species to become extinct (e.,g., Dinosaurs, dodos etc.). There is no reason why people should try to prevent this from happening. Do you agree or disagree?

It is essence for animal species to die out over time as part of the natural cycle of life. However, the issue of whether people should endeavour to prevent animal species from becoming extinct is a highly debated topic. Some argue that it is a natural process that has been occurring for millennia, while others believe that humans have a moral responsibility to protect endangered species. In my opinion, I disagree with the statement that there is no reason for people to make an effort to prevent the extinction of animal species.

To begin with, not only does every species play a crucial role in maintaining the delicate balance of ecosystems, but they also contribute to the overall health of the planet. In other words, creatures provide various benefits to sustainability of our planet in numerous ways. For example, bees are essential pollinators that help plants reproduce, this is especially it is important for many crops, while predators such as wolves help control the population of prey species. As a result, if these species were to become extinct, it could have far-reaching detrimental consequences for the environment.

Furthermore, the extinction of animal species can also have a direct impact on human life. To put this another way, they contribute to human society, its health, well-being and economic development. For instance, many medicines and other useful resources like food, clothes are derived from plants and animals, and the loss of certain species could lead to a decrease in medical advancements and economic opportunities.  Consequently, humanity could face a host of issues such as scarcity of clean water, food and other valuable resources.

In conclusion, while it is true that extinction is a natural process, it is important for people to try to save all animal species. Animals play a crucial role in maintaining ecosystems and biodiversity, which ultimately benefits human society by providing clean air and water, fertile soil, and natural resources.  Their loss could have negative affect on human life. Therefore, efforts should be made to protect endangered species and preserve biodiversity for future generations.

exam_question: Some believe that because everyone needs a place to live, governments should provide houses for those who are too poor to afford their own. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
There has been a controversy over whether governments should provide free or affordable housing for those who are homeless. In my opinion, while governments are responsible for assisting the homeless, I firmly believe that providing free or low-cost housing is not the most effective solution.

Housing is a fundamental human right, and the government should ensure that all citizens have access to safe living conditions. If the government takes responsibility for this, there would be multiple benefits. Firstly, providing accommodation can reduce crime rates. When individuals have stable housing, they are less likely to engage in criminal activities due to financial hardship. In this regard, the government should introduce policies that offer financial assistance to those who cannot afford housing. This would not only decrease homelessness but also help prevent the poverty cycle that often leads to criminal behaviour. Secondly, ensuring access to housing would allow people to allocate more resources towards physical activity, as their financial burdens would be lighter. Research has shown that when the government supports housing, such as providing financial assistance for homeownership, it increases  participation in physical activities, which ultimately enhances productivity and public health.

However, despite the economic benefits of government housing assistance, there are significant downsides to this policy. If the government continues to invest heavily in free or low-cost housing, it could adversely affect the development of critical infrastructure. For example, in Taiwan, while the government’s housing support program has helped the poor, it has led to a reduction in funding for essential public services, such as sports facilities. In Taipei City, where the population is large, the lack of public sports centres has significantly limited access to physical exercise. A report showed that exercise participation has decreased by 20%, which in turn has reduced work efficiency and overall productivity. Therefore, many experts suggest that the government should prioritize investing in other sectors, such as healthcare, education, and infrastructure, in order to support long-term social development.

In conclusion, while it is essential for governments to assist the homeless, I strongly believe that providing free or low-cost housing is not the best approach. The government should instead focus on long-term solutions, such as investing in public sports facilities, healthcare, and education, which would help create a healthier and more self-sufficient society.

exam_question: Some people think that governments should invest mainly in making public transportation faster while other think there are more important priorities (cost, the environment). Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

If governments invested more in environmentally friendly forms of transportation, such as cycling, our cities would be less polluted and more harmonious with nature.

In conclusion, I understand why people might want to have faster public transportation, but it seems to me that an eco-friendly transport system is much more desirable for our health and our planet.

exam_question: If a product is good and meets customer needs, then people will buy it and advertising is unnecessary. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:

exam_question: A Rise In The Standard Of Living In A Country Often Only Seems To Benefit Cities Rather Than Rural Areas. What problems can this cause? How might these problems be reduced?
text:

To cope up with these pressing issues in the cities, the government requires spreading awareness about the consequences of the deforestation as well as high level of air pollution. Moreover, implementing odd-even rule that allows only even or odd number vehicles to run on the road and encouraging the people to prefer the car pool should be a prudent approach. The government also needs to create more job opportunities in the villages. They should also build good educational institutions. If people can find jobs in their native place they will not move to cities and when they continue to live in their villages, facilities will start becoming available there as well.

In conclusion, overpopulation in the cities may lead to irreversible effects on the environment and can cause difficulty for the people to earn a living. However, if the government and the people join hands, they can mitigate these issues to a great extent and achieve even development throughout the country.

exam_question: Computer games are very popular for all ages and nationalities. Parents think this has little educational value and it will be harmful to children. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

exam_question: It is a natural process for animal species to become extinct (e.g. Dinosaurs, dodos, etc.) There is no reason why people should try to prevent this from happening. Do you agree or disagree?
text:
With an increasing number of animals enlisted in protection catalogues, there has been a dissent that extinction is a natural process with which people should not interfere. In my view, the opinion overemphasises the importance of Darwinism so that overlooks people's determination to preserve themselves by protecting endangered animals.

Although the passage endeavours to defend people's efforts to prevent extinction, the supporters of Darwinism are also with some reasons. For illustration, they are reasonable in claiming that if people disproportionately intervene in natural progress, consequences are usually beyond control. One compelling example is seen in Australia, where the scientists once contrived to save land parrots from extinction by introducing foxes as the natural enemies of rats, which ate land parrots' eggs. However, contrary to the original expectation, the foxes introduced found land parrots were better prey, which worsened the situation of land parrots and consequently accelerated the extinction of the species. In light of this, it seems plausible to claim that people's efforts will only exacerbate situations, and they ought to be satisfied with the role of observers.

However, this perspective to a large degree neglects people's determination to refuse tamely submit their future to  nature. The modern society is highly dependent on bio-products, food, medicine, or textile. For example, it is inconceivable to produce fruits without bees, and therefore if  humans allow natural selection to exterminate bees, if humans show "respect" for Darwinism, it is not different from committing suicide. In light of this, the passage is inclined to view the human's endeavours to prevent extinction as an effort to take control of our own future, which actually is what humans have done across millions, using the brain to emerge from nature.

In summary, the passage can understand the apprehension of the supporters of Darwinism, as there are some examples of people's intervention in natural selection brought undesirable consequences. Despite this, if we forsake these efforts, it equals to submit ourselves totally to nature's control, which is more undesirable, and therefore the human had better continue to explore along the road of stopping extinction.

exam_question: Advice for Medical Problems Some people today prefer to get advice for medical problems and do not want to visit a doctor. Why is this? Is this a positive or a negative development?
text:
It can be generally observed that many people today prefer to seek answers to their medical problems online, instead of traditionally going to their GP straight away. It cannot be denied that the advance of the internet has drastically changed people’s behaviour, including how people choose to seek information about medical issues. Not only people choose to use the internet to find more information about their symptoms, some people also decide to forego seeing a medical professional altogether. Since a vast number of internet sources are available to people with a click of a finger, it seems quite logical to assume that internet users would take advantage of all the unlimited resources available online when it comes to medical concerns. For instance, if a regular user of the internet would develop a rash it seems only reasonable that the person in question would most definitely google their symptoms and try to pin down the possible causes, name of the condition and available treatments.

 

The use of search engines to gain some perspective about your medical symptoms only becomes a danger when people decide to substitute the sources available on the internet for a professional diagnosis. When people decide to self-diagnose their symptoms on the internet without seeing a doctor, this could potentially result in a number of harmful, damaging consequences that could have been avoided. For example, because of their lack of knowledge and medical training, people could misdiagnose a medical condition and as a result, make it worse. People could also mistake a serious condition for something else and in turn waste a lot of time that could be essential in order to seek professional help.

 

In conclusion, the availability of medical resources on the internet has contributed to people looking up their medical symptoms online and this phenomenon could only be harmful when people decide to substitute this for a professional diagnosis.

exam_question: In the past, knowledge was contained in books. Nowadays, knowledge is uploaded to the internet. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages

In conclusion, using the internet as an educational resource may pose several disadvantages, such as addiction and the possibility of sharing valuable content. However, the benefits are much more significant, including convenience and a reduction in your expenses.

exam_question: 3 Aban/ Some people believe that it is good to share as much information as possible in scientific research, business, and the academic world. exam_question: Large companies use sport events to promote their products. Some people think this has a negative impact on sports. To what extent do you agree or disagree

exam_question: In many countries, people now wear Western clothes such as suits and jeans rather than traditional clothing. Why is this the case? Is this a positive or negative development?
text:
The prevalence of Western-style clothes in the wardrobes of people is an increasingly noticeable trend in contemporary society in a lot of countries. This essay aims to explore the reasons behind this phenomenon and discuss its potential impacts.

There are two reasons for this tendency. One major reason is the globalized culture we live in today. Thanks to advanced technology and transportation, people can easily access information and products from other parts of the world, including fashion trends. As a consequence, western clothing styles have become more accessible and appealing to youngsters who seek diversity and individuality in their attire. Another factor that contributes to this tendency is the influence of media and popular culture. Celebrities, influencers, and movie characters often wear Western-style outfits, which set fashion trends and shape people’s perceptions of what is fashionable. As a result, many citizens emulate these styles, perceiving them as symbols of modernity and sophistication.

However, whether this trend is positive or negative depends on one’s perspective. On the positive side, it reflects cultural exchange and globalization, enabling citizens to appreciate different aesthetics and broaden their horizons. Moreover, it offers youngsters greater choices in expressing themselves through their clothing. On the other hand, some argue that excessive reliance on Western-style clothing could lead to a loss of traditional values and cultural identity. It might also contribute to consumerism, where individuals prioritize material possessions over deeper values like spirituality and interpersonal relationships.

In conclusion, the increasing preference for Western-style clothing among people results from globalization and media influences. While this trend has its advantages, it may also carry potential risks. Therefore, it is essential to maintain a balance between appreciating diverse cultures and preserving our own traditions.

exam_question: In the past, knowledge was contained in books. Nowadays, knowledge is uploaded to the internet. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
text:
It is a fact of modern life that most information today is stored online, rather than in physical books as it was in the past. In my opinion, this is a negative overall despite its obvious conveniences.

Supporters of this trend can point to the numerous ways knowledge kept online can be disseminated and used. Online information is almost universally accessible, narrowing socioeconomic differences in society and allowing for various conveniences. First of all, users can find relevant information on search engines from a wide range of sources including user-generated sites like Wikipedia to news outlets like The New York Times and academic journals as well. Once an individual locates the information they are looking for, it is also easier to search within that article, share it with others, have it wherever they go and store more than would be possible if it were a hard copy.

Nonetheless, storing information online encourages the dependence on computer technology that is harmful to the human mind. In the past, if a person wanted to research a given topic, they would have to check out a library book or talk with an expert. This process was much slower and open to the possibility of bias. However, it also meant that individuals were more conscientious and patiently learned from fuller, more nuanced sources. Nowadays, most people read short articles, hastily written to attract more clicks and generate advertising revenue. These tap into a fundamental human need to be constantly engaged and feeling pleasure. Over time, this has led to a generation addicted to devices, lacking the healthy habits engendered by careful research and study.

In conclusion, despite the handiness of online information, the impact on the human psyche makes this a negative trend on the level. Individuals must find ways to counter these potentially injurious effects.

exam_question: LIVING IN A COUNTRY WHERE YOU HAVE TO SPEAK A FOREIGN LANGUAGE CAN CAUSE SERIOUS SOCIAL PROBLEMS, AS WELL AS PRACTICAL PROBLEMS. TO WHAT EXTENT DO YOU AGREE OR DISAGREE WITH THIS STATEMENT?
text:
One of the issues faced by people living in foreign land is the language barrier, which can be challenging in some aspects. I somewhat agree with the statement in question. Many social problems arise due to this, but because of advancements in technology, this is not as big a problem practically as it used to be up until a few years ago.
Since language is a fundamental part of communication, a barrier makes it difficult to interact with people in a society. Adjusting in an unfamiliar place requires human interaction and bonding. This cannot be fully achieved if a communication gap exists. For instance, in my country Pakistan where Urdu is spoken, foreigners have a hard time making friends, having interpersonal relationships with colleagues etc. And until they learn the native language, this social awkwardness can be very troublesome for them. Therefore, there is no doubt that social problems do arise because of language dissimilarity when living abroad.
Innovations in technology have really helped in overcoming the problems faced by people living in a country where a foreign language is spoken. Nowadays, smart phones can be used to translate almost any word or phrase. Though a little time consuming, there are multiple apps which provide us with accurate translations along with audio to avoid pronunciation errors. Social media apps like Facebook also have multiple language options. Thus, a person’s everyday activities are not hindered if such tools are used efficiently. 
To conclude, having to speak a foreign language can be socially problematic because of the communication gap. However, technological advancements have minimized the practical day-to-day issues.

exam_question: People are annoyed or entertained by advertising but they are not affected by advertisements when making shopping decisions. To what extent you agree or disagree?
text:
People may go through different feelings when seeing an ad on a television, whether feel engaged or irritated by them, however, it may not impact them when they want to purchase a good. Although some individuals may be influenced by the hyperboles said about one purchase and be affected while buying what they wish, I believe most people ignore advertisements while buying.

Critics of the viewpoint that people do not care about ads point out that advertisement makes buying enticing. In fact, when buyers search through sites and come across an item which is beneficial for them, them may go for it. What matters for people while making a shopping decision is its advantages, and as many experts are recruited by some companies to talk about their products positively, people might be affected and consider buying them. Additionally, offering discounts can motivate people to opt for some items that are advertised. A person that has seen an ad showing what he wishes with a 20 or 30% discount, he would be affected, thus taking it into consideration while purchasing.

Nonetheless, people try to buy items wisely and prioritize their needs. Indeed, a wide range of people go shopping, but return with only one or two necessary items. They have foster a sense that advertisements try to pursue them to buy some unnecessary items that are actually unimportant and do not meet their needs. Furthermore, age bracket of people is of utmost importance for them while making a shopping decision. The disposable income of people may discourage them to be influence by some ads even though they may have a craving for them. A person with an income of three thousand dollars cannot typically buy items based on ads because of financial boundaries they have. Having spent their income on household or other important needs, they are left with minimum income and do not pay any attention on ads for buying an item.

To conclude, despite the fact that many may be influenced by advertisements while want to buy items, believing they could benefit them, I assert that people are more aware of their basic needs, and based of their priority and income bracket, make authentic decisions.

exam_question: In recent time economic growth has made some people richer in both developed and developing countries. While studies show that people in developing countries are happier now than before, people in developed countries are no happier than they were before.
text:
Nobody can deny the growing economic progress in both developing and developed nations thanks to globalization and the advent of high technology. In recent years, while people living in developing countries are more content with their life than those in the past, people residing in developed countries cope with the contrary phenomenon. Basically, there’re many reasons for this phenomenon and we will discuss the issue here. 

There is no doubt that happiness is the key factor that makes people’s life more valuable. Obviously, people from developing nations, nowadays, can have higher living standards in comparison with their previous dwellers. In these countries, money plays a fundamental role in their daily life. With the rapid development of every life aspect, they strive to attain salary increments or financial rewards that enable them to escape from poverty. As a result, they become wealthier and feel happier in their life.

It is true that enjoying our lives with our beloved people, along with other welfare benefits, appears to be among the great prerequisites for the desired life apart from working and earning a living. Jan-Emmanuel De Neve, Oxford University economist, and WHR collaborator says: “In terms of policy, we always feel that developing for the sake of growth cannot be considered the happiness of mankind." From that perspective, one can figure out such valuable lessons about happiness. For one thing, financial adequacy is indispensable. Without money, many people will have to lead a poor life and feel extreme fatigue all the time. As a result, people are often under constant pressure and cannot live happily as their counterparts who remain financially stable. In order to sustain the staff’s lives at the basic level, governments should support them by providing more job opportunities, greater subsidies during difficult times such as a global pandemic or economic crisis, or greater grants in case of healthcare issues. 

 On the other hand, high competitiveness in the economy and target-related problems in modern society are factors that people are not happy about. Due to economic growth, companies have to compete fiercely against each other for the market. Therefore, employees are forced to work harder than before so that the company will not be overtaken by other companies in technology, quality, and quantity. In addition to the hectic life that they are supposed to lead, their performance at work is frequently assessed to reduce the risk of redundancy if the companies restructure or downsize. To illustrate, companies specializing in technology, and furniture, ... have to regularly update the market situation to attract customers by creating new designs and technologies. When the competition among companies becomes intense, the workers will have to put more effort into their work to get a lot of tasks done. Subsequently, such poor work-life balance will make people in developed countries no longer as happy as they used to be.

All in all, although it seems logical to accept certain reasons why more and more people have become materialistic, chasing a rich life without caring about the existing, good things around them, other aspects of life including environmental, social, and welfare issues also need to be closely taken notice of to ensure the ultimate sustainability. Human life is limited, what can be better to fulfil personal wishes as well as improve our living quality than spending more time for ourselves, travelling, discovering ourselves, nurturing our interests, and taking good care of our health. A matter of greater importance is that employers should offer their staff the dramatic availability of opportunities to enjoy their every moment of life.

exam_question: More and more students at university today are not choosing to study science. Why is this happening? What are the effects of it?
text:
Recent years have witnessed an increasing number of students opting for other subjects rather than science. This essay will shed light on the underlying reasons behind this phenomenon before highlighting several negative consequences of this trend. 

The tendency of students towards not choosing to study science can be attributed to two main reasons. One significant reason revolves around the demanding nature of the curriculum coupled with prohibitive tuition fees. Not only does it require students to have a thorough understanding of complex concepts but also charges higher tuition fees compared to other subjects owing to the necessity for specialised technological equipment involved. This may deter prospective students from applying if they do not have additional financial support or scholarships. Additionally, the perception of limited applicability. In this digital age, subjects like marketing or business administration are perceived as broader career opportunities across various industries. Meanwhile, studying science focuses on the study of theoretical knowledge and research in the laboratory, which makes one only able to work in science-related industries.

The dwindling interest among students in studying science can give rise to far-reaching repercussions. Chief among these is the loss of innovations, making industries reliant on scientific advancements may struggle to find qualified professionals. This shortage could result in lower innovation and technological advancement, hindering progress in key areas such as healthcare and environmental protection. In addition to this, the diminishing interest in science may exacerbate the existing lack of diversity in the job market. Since people are inclined to steer away from science, the range of available professions would shrink and potentially limit career options for future generations as a consequence. 

In conclusion, the issue of more students opting out of science is driven by its demanding learning journey, tuition fees and applicability. This issue will contribute to the lack of innovations for certain industries and reduce the diversity in the job market.

exam_question: Many people today are choosing to travel to other countries. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
text:
More and more people today are choosing to travel internationally. This positive development is mainly because of a rise in middle class income coupled with advances in aviation.

People today can afford to travel as it has become more convenient. The last half century has seen wages in both developed and developing companies climb with the concomitant expansion of the global middle class. Workers have the disposable income to travel that they lacked in the past. This has been complemented with safer airplanes so individuals are not afraid to fly. Airfares have also become cheaper as companies like Boeing produce more efficient planes, competition intensifies between competing airlines, and the supply more than meets demand for flights. These factors combined have spawned a golden age of international travel.

Looking at the opportunity in perspective, it is hard to see the advent of international travel as anything less than one of mankind’s greatest achievements. For the entirety of human history, most people lived and died near where they were born. Anyone who wanted to travel to another country had to possess enormous wealth, time, and courage. Today, the average employee can save up and travel to see the wonders of the Rennaissance in Southern Europe, the vast monuments of history and modernity in China, or explore any other corner of the Earth that has piqued their interest. This is an unprecedented opportunity unavailable to past generations.

In conclusion, international travel is a byproduct of the modern age and we should all be grateful for its possibility. There are clear environmental drawbacks, but those should not blind people to its benefits taken as a whole.

exam_question: A rise in the standard of living in a country often only seems to benefit cities rather than rural areas. What problems can this cause and how might these problems be reduced?

exam_question: People these days watch TV, films and other programes alone rather than with other people. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
text:
