On the other hand, there are some individuals who assert that travelling is advantageous for student's personal growth. That is because when exploring new countries and cultures enables youngsters to broaden their horizons about the world as well as to step out of their norm, which is a stepping stone for them to build up confidence. While this point has credibility, it also comes with the cost of solitude feelings and unforeseen challenges that can exacerbate student's travel experience unless there is  proper preparedness for the journey. Thus, gaining experience from working is a more sustainable option for  teens compared to travelling.

In conclusion, skills provision and financial independence encourage students to get working experience rather than go travelling since travelling may contain hidden risks. Ultimately, this essay has proved that gaining working experience is more important than travelling.

exam_question: It is now possible for scientists and tourists to travel to remote natural environments, such as South pole. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
text:

Since going to other cities or countries has been too common for most people, it might be more exciting for them to explore new places such as the South Pole or the Amazon rainforest. Furthermore, when visiting remote areas, visitors might acquire more knowledge about the natural habitat as well as have deeper insights into species. For instance, when going to the North Pole, scientists can learn about the life of polar bears, which live far away from humans. This newfound knowledge can be a precursor to clinical breakthroughs or provide scientists with comprehensive insights to more effectively deal with environmental issues such as climate change. 

Conversely, regarding the disadvantages, there are significant negative related to the environment when scientists and tourists travel to the remote natural environment. The first one is that travelling to remote natural areas can be risky if the travelers are not adequately prepared because health services or hospitals in these places might not be available or limited. For example, the temperature at the South Pole is usually very low, which adversely affects people’s health. Travelling to forests can also be dangerous as people have to face the risk of being attacked by animals. In conclusion, I believe the disadvantages of people being able to travel to remote areas outweigh its advantages.

exam_question: The increase in the production of consumer goods results in damage to the natural environment. What are the causes of this? What can be done to solve this problem ?

In support of this reason, a known fact is that the growing demand for products like smartphones has triggered extensive mining for rare minerals, contributing to environmental degradation. Another problematic cause is the excessive use of single-use plastics, which greatly contributes to environmental pollution. For instance, the disposal of plastic products leads to significant waste production, including non-biodegradable materials that harm the environment.

Seeing the Challenge with a brighter mind, many solutions can be helpful to curb this menace. One of the solutions is implementing laws to limit resource use and promote sustainable consumption practices. Secondly, incentivizing recycling and proper waste disposal can significantly reduce environmental pollution. Lastly, promoting alternatives to single-use plastics, such as reusable bags and containers, can further mitigate the dilemma.

In summary, the problem arises from multiple factors, including the increasing demand for consumer goods and the overreliance on disposable plastics. The primary responsibility for solving this issue rests with both governments and individuals, who must adopt more sustainable consumption habits and practices.

exam_question: Some people think that newly built houses should follow the style of old houses in local areas. Others think that people should have freedom to build houses of their own styles. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
text:
A highly contentious view at issue is whether newly erected dwellings are required to conform to existing structural standards in the vicinity or the property owners are at complete liberty to build their place of residence. This essay will elaborate on both angles of the dispute before coming to a reasoned conclusion.  

On the one hand, those who advocate the resemblance of vernacular architecture claim that it helps preserve the visual and tangible features of cultural identity, which is therefore inclined to boost local tourism. That is to say, as architecture is one characteristic of cultural heritage with which people can interact and adapt, duplicating available old styles would ensure the character of the neighborhood remain intact, hence, acting as repositories of traditional legacy. A prime example can be seen in the ancient city of Hue in Vietnam, where this happens to be the case, most notably with its garden houses reminiscent of feudal architecture. The fact that these exotic garden houses in themselves record the pieces of previous generations’ stories, which fill visitors with nostalgia and take them aback by its elegance, results in a massive influx of tourists on a regular basis. To the proponents of the idea, this justification is quite convincing. 

On the other hand, albeit the stance above, the ardent defenders of the originality point to the power of free will as a primary cause for concern. To be more specific, most people in their entire life can only afford a once-in-a-lifetime shelter where they feel comfortable going back and forth. Since homeowners are the chief beneficiary who are directly impacted, having their permanent abode in accordance with their aesthetic liking is the centerpiece which not only gives them a sense of wellbeing but also lifts their spirits. This being the case, their rights would be surely infringed were they forced to construct their homes following the stipulations against their wishes. Having considered that, this argument as well tends to be fairly powerful. 

On balance, whilst there are valid opinions from differing perspectives on this controversial debate, my conviction is that architectural styles of home construction in personal preference would be an infinitely favored option

exam_question: Large companies should pay higher salaries to CEOs and executives compared with other workers. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:

Firstly, CEOs and executives often have more responsibilities and face greater pressure in running a large company. These individuals are responsible for making critical decisions that affect the success and growth of the company. Hence, it is reasonable to reward them with higher salaries, as they play a vital role in leading the company towards prosperity. Moreover, these key personnel are required to possess a broad range of skills and extensive knowledge, which have often been acquired through years of experience and education. Recognizing and compensating them adequately for these skills and knowledge is justifiable.

Furthermore, paying higher salaries to top-level management can be seen as a way to attract and retain talented individuals. Competition among companies is fierce, and in order to recruit the best talent in the industry, competitive compensation packages are often required. Highly talented individuals have the option to choose from multiple job offers, and companies must offer attractive rewards to ensure that they choose their organization. To remain competitive, companies need the best individuals at the helm, and offering higher salaries to CEOs and executives is a way to achieve this.

However, it is important to strike a balance and ensure that the wage gap between CEOs and executives and other workers does not become too excessive. While it is true that top management personnel play a crucial role in the success of the company, it is equally important to acknowledge the contributions of other employees. The efforts of workers at all levels contribute to the overall performance of the company, and their dedication and hard work should also be recognized. A large wage gap between top executives and other workers can create feelings of inequality and demotivation among the workforce, which can have a negative impact on company morale and productivity.

In conclusion, I agree that large companies should pay higher salaries to CEOs and executives compared to other workers due to their increased responsibilities and talents. However, it is crucial to maintain a fair and reasonable wage gap to ensure equity and harmony among all employees.

exam_question: The increase in the production of consumer goods results in damage to the natural environment. What are the causes of this? What can be done to solve this problem?
text:
By the present, there have been many concerns about the environment negatively affected to by human activities, and one of them is the consumer goods manufacturing. It is essential to argue how this manufacturing has negative impact to the environment and what should be done to restrict this impact. 

To begin with, consumer goods companies are responsible for the pollution. They try their best to reduce expenses to maximize profits. Because dealing with production waste is extravagant for many companies, they decide to skip this activity and emit them into the environment. There are many consequences of this decision to the environment. The majority of companies use fossil fuels as the main energy source and several toxic gases such as carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxide and sulfur dioxide are emitted into the air. Because of them, air quality can decrease, impacting to photosynthesis of plants and respiration of animals. In addition, many studies indicate that the three aforementioned gases are the main cause of greenhouse effect, resulting in global warming and climate change. Another concerning consequence is the gases can result in acid rain, destroying many species in nature. As regard to water, it can be affected by liquid waste from factories, including wastewater, sludge, oil and grease. Water species can die due to these pollutants or have to migrate to other habitats. To reduce these consequences, government should impose taxation on contaminating activities of companies and taxes should be as high as possible. By this way, factories have to consider whether not dealing with waste is still beneficial for them. If companies keep this behavior, they can face strict tax punishments, which can make their products exorbitant and affect to their profit.

However, companies are not the only factor of environmental problems. Consumers are also the accomplice in the matter. Nowadays, there is a tendency among them that they use disposable goods instead of durable goods. For instance, customers are more likely to use plastic-wrapped paper cups, not conventional plastic, glass or porcelain mugs just because they want to use once only and then throw into trash bins. The trend is also apparent in using plates, people prefer the plastic-wrapped paper, not the typical plastic or the porcelain. Consequently, landfills will have to receive a great amount of garbage of disposable goods. The problem is the majority of these goods are made of materials which are usually difficult to decompose in short periods and toxic when incinerated. Therefore, people are likely to keep garbage in landfills. It is certain that land can get contaminated due to the consumption behavior of modern society. To restrict land pollution, government should impose taxes on disposable goods. Due to taxation, these goods’ costs increase and consumers are more likely to restrict using them. By this solution, the amount of waste from disposable goods can decline. 

In conclusion, the production of consumer goods impacts to the natural environment through companies, by waste, and customers, by using disposable goods. To reduce these negative effects, governments should impose taxes on waste and disposable goods. Due to taxation, companies and consumers have to think again about the possible benefits and losses they have, indirectly reducing their influence on the environment.

There are two major positive effects to this including collecting materials that are vital for research and adding more places to visitors' travelling lists, I am of the opinion that the drawbacks consisting of a rise in pollution and an adverse bearing on indigenous residents will be likely more significant. 

On the one hand, travelling to remote destinations can bring certain benefits. Chief of these is that these isolated places might have more materials which are crucial for research. By travelling to these sites, scientists are enabled to gain access to an enormous amount of information such as geographical structures, unique species and climate patterns. Hence, travelling to these regions can give them  valuable experiences and unforgettable memories.

On the other hand, I firmly believe that the downsides of visiting less explored lands can overshadow the positive aspects. The first one is that travelling to these regions can cause a rise in pollution. Given the fact that many popular attractions are already polluted with tourists’ waste, it is readily apparent that nothing can make sure this will not happen again to newly-discovered areas. For instance, the Amazon rainforest used to be lush and verdant, however owing to the development of tourism, more waste such as bottles or nylon bags has  been released into the environment; thereby, the Amazon rainforest is more likely to be destroyed. Furthermore, other activities might have an adverse bearing on indigenous residents. When pollution is increasingly prevalent in these zones, it can breed poor sanitation, which affects locals’ health. Consequently, it can facilitate diseases to spread among local inhabitants.

In conclusion, while visiting faraway lands can bring new materials for research and expand people’s travelling lists; I suppose that this tendency can be detrimental due to the rise of pollution and the undesirable effects on local people.

exam_question: Society is based on rules and laws. It could not function if individuals were free to do whatever they wanted. To what extent do you agree or disagree with these opinions?

Take Vietnam as an example. In the past, Vietnamese women were prohibited from voting. However, they are now free to cast their ballots as permitted by laws. Secondly, laws protect us from discrimination against our race, gender, age, or disability. Without any laws, basic human rights were not safeguarded, which might result in resentment and even rebellion.

In conclusion, it seems to me that laws play an indispensable part in making the world a safer place and ensure the basic human rights of each citizen. Therefore, a lawless community would inevitably endanger the well-being of its member and threaten the social fabric.

exam_question: The increase in the production of consumer goods results in damage to the natural environment. What are the causes of this? What can be done to solve this problem? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
text:
In the century of technological advances, there is a high demand for consumer goods in the market. Therefore, many companies aim to manufacture a tremendous number of products to compete with their rival companies. However, while striving for more profit, CEOs often overlook the negative impact of production on the environment, such as greenhouse gas emissions and soil acidification. These issues can be mitigated through restrictions on the production of non-essential consumer goods and the development of an optimal recycling system.

First and foremost, the environment suffers from greenhouse gases - byproducts of the manufacturing process like methane, carbon dioxide, and other gases. These emissions contribute to global warming, resulting in rising sea levels, wildfires, and other natural disasters. To prevent the adverse effects of human activity, each country's production sector should limit its manufacturing levels. For instance, governments can impose restrictions on the supply of less essential consumer goods. Undoubtedly, limiting production may lead to increased inflation and potential economic crises; however, preserving nature must remain a top priority.

Secondly, scraps from factories negatively affect the land and its components. Discarded waste accumulates in vast landfills, leading to soil acidification. As a result, the soil becomes unsuitable for plant growth, disrupting the ecosystem. Herbivores face food shortages (plants), and their predators, in turn, struggle to find prey due to these deaths, leading to increased competition for available resources. Consequently, the entire ecosystem suffers, eventually leading to its destruction. To address this issue, people should develop a robust recycling system, which will reduce the volume of garbage and help neutralize the soil.

In conclusion, humanity is an integral part of the living ecosystem, and environmental issues directly affect our surroundings. Pursuing profit at the expense of the environment can have devastating consequences. Greenhouse gas emissions and soil acidification pose significant threats to the ecosystem. Therefore, addressing these problems by limiting production and establishing recycling facilities is of paramount importance for the well-being of future generations.

exam_question: Some people think that the best way to improve road safety is to increase the minimum legal age for driving a car or motorbike. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
text:
Some people believe that raising the minimum driving age is the best solution to enhance road safety. I disagree with this idea because I believe that other methods are equally important and should be taken into account as well.

On the one hand, I agree that increasing the minimum age for getting a driving licence can be an eﬀective road safety measure. Firstly, since people are often more mature and have more life experience when they get older, they can make quicker and wiser decisions to avoid dangerous situations on the road compared to younger drivers. My father, for example, will never use his phone when driving as he knows that he could easily lose his concentration and cause an accident. Secondly, raising the minimum driving age can allow adolescents to have more time to sharpen their driving skills. They can attend defensive driving courses to learn how to deal with diﬀerent driving scenarios, which will help them minimize the risk of accidents when driving in the future.

On the other hand, I think that better road safety can be achieved by other more eﬀective methods without increasing the driving age. To begin with, more stringent traffic regulations should be imposed, which would act as a deterrent to would-be traffic law breakers. In Singapore, people who run red lights are fined heavily, and therefore this will make them more responsible in order to avoid future punishments. In addition, governments should allocate financial resources to improving public transport, which would encourage citizens to drive their private cars or motorbikes less. As a result, these residents will no longer worry about the risks that they may face when driving their own vehicles, such as drunk driving or falling asleep at the wheel.

In conclusion, while raising the legal driving age can make our roads safer to some extent, I believe that governments should also introduce other road safety measures that are discussed above.

exam_question: Some people think that it is a waste of time for high school students to study literature, such as novels and poems. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
Many today claim that learning about literature should no longer be a key component of the high school curriculum. In my opinion, there are practical reasons for this sentiment but literature still serves a purpose.

Proponents of this reform argue other subjects deserve prioritisation. There is little doubt that in the 21st century, the most important subjects for students’ future careers related to the sciences, such as engineering and computer science, or the practical humanities, like a business. The earlier that students begin specialising, the more likely they are to have a head start on the competition and secure a well-paying job immediately after graduating high school or university. In contrast, the novels and poems that students read in high school are usually completely forgotten within a few years and do not teach any tangible skills that will help them advance in the real world.

Nonetheless, the literature contains many of the most important and fundamental truths about the human condition. Life is about more than a career and great authors tackle the most fundamental philosophical and psychological questions. For example, the masters of 19th century Russian literature, including Tolstoy and Dostoevsky, are primarily concerned with human psychology and how this fits into a larger context of man’s search for meaning. Their exploration of these issues is relevant to everyone and cannot be replaced with a steady career. Moreover, the way in which great writers develop their themes, the aesthetic quality of their writing itself, imparts to careful readers the importance of artistic expression and may help them see outside the narrow modern confines of accumulating the most material wealth.

In conclusion, the utilitarian benefits of studying practical subjects do not outweigh the deeper values of literature. It is therefore advisable that literature be emphasised in high school classrooms.

exam_question: Climate change is a phenomenon that affects countries all over the world. Many people strongly believe that it is the responsibility of individuals, rather than corporations and government, to deal with this problem. To what extent do you agree?

Individuals can only contribute in small ways, such as take public transportation, choose product with less packaging, and recycle as much as possible. On the other hand, the government have the power to enact legislation that requires individuals and large corporation to obey certain restrictions. Besides, the government could also invest in renewable energy generations, such as solar, wind, or waterpower.
To sum up, although individuals may have a role to play in combating climate change, the government should take up the rightful burden by taking measures to rein in corporate and private waste.

exam_question: Some people think that newly built houses should follow the style of the old houses in the local areas, while others think that people should have freedom to build houses of their own styles. Discuss both views and give your own opinion?
text:

While there are some benefits of building consistently old-style houses, from my own standpoint, I lean towards the latter idea of building new houses differently.

On the one hand, it is obvious that a row of old-style houses brings a certain number of advantages to the local area. First, the erection of new houses having the same style as the old ones contributes to the architectural identity of a town, which would help develop the local tourism industry. Second, maintaining the old style also allows local people to preserve their cultural heritage. A typical example of this view is Hoi An old village which is renowned for rows of yellow-painted and tile-roof houses, generating a unique architectural style. Such ancient patterns not only keep cultural values enduring with the locals to this day but also boost the development of the tourism industry which seems to bring a huge amount of money to both local authorities and residents.

On the other hand, other people support the idea of building new-style houses. The apparent merit of this idea is that constructing houses with different new styles would satisfy people’s imagination and creativity. Indeed, the public has their own preferences for house design. For example, while some people are in favour of the Mediterranean design attaching great importance to the features of refreshment and harmony with nature, others may prefer a warm atmosphere created by wooden walls, furniture and ornaments. exam_question: Some people think the newly built houses should be the same as the old house style in local areas. Others argue that local authorities should allow people to build houses in their own styles. Discuss both views and give your opinion
text:
It is argued that the architectural style of new buildings should be in accordance with existing buildings in an area, while others believe that people should have the freedom to design their own house.  While there are some valid arguments for uniformity in architecture, I agree that buildings’ designs should not be too heavily regulated.

On the one hand, there are many reasons to require new buildings to follow the styles of existing structures. Advocates of this view believe that it would be better for heritage sites  if certain aesthetic features are followed by housing contractors. For example, Venice, one of  Italy’s most popular cities, is well-loved for its Gothic architecture with domed cathedrals and cobblestone arch bridges. Such harmonious building styles would not have been possible without strict building codes. Besides, a homogenous architecture style will ensure that people already living in an area will not be affected negatively by new structures. To be specific, in a town where terraced houses are predominant, constructing a tall and wide apartment complex can compromise or even damage the structural integrity of existing buildings.

On the other hand, I would argue that people should enjoy a certain degree of freedom when building their houses. First, a diversity in architectural styles does not take away the beauty of an area. In fact, some  of the world's most stunning cities - Tokyo, New York, and Singapore - feature varying urbanscapes with skyscrapers as well as classical architectures. These places can attract tourists from all over the world while still offering a variety of architecture styles.  Conversely, forcing people to adopt a uniform style of building can make a neighborhood look boring and uninspired. For example, many planned suburbs which take a cookie-cutter approach to architecture look sterile and identical compared to a naturally developed city. 

In conclusion, although it is necessary to maintain some degree of architectural consistency in a historically important site, I still believe that modern buildings should be allowed to be unique to create more aesthetic diversity in an area.

exam_question: Some think that students must travel to another country in order to learn its language and customs. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
Many believe that in order to become immersed in another language and culture it is important to travel to the country in question. I agree generally, though there are certain exceptions depending on the purpose for learning.

Those with an academic interest in a given culture often do not need to travel there. This is particularly true if they are researching an historic period. For example, a scholar learning about Ancient Greece going there today, will only see ruins and a radically different culture. Ancient Greek is no longer even spoken. It would be much more profitable for a student of the Ancients to learn the language fluently on their own and become steeped in their histories and classic literature. The works of Euripides, Sophocles and Herodotus will provide far greater insight into the history, culture, and language of the Ancient Greeks than the few vestiges from thousands of years ago still standing today.

Nonetheless, cases like the one detailed above are rare and most people will benefit greatly from a more immersive experience. The difference between those studying abroad and learning in their own country is illustrative. Students attempting to learn English, for example, will need to be naturally adept at languages to become fluent without living in an English-speaking country. The majority of learners will improve faster when making daily transactions in English and learning in the real world outside the classroom. The cultural advantages are also self-evident. English movies and TV shows are realistic to varying degrees but pale in comparison to having actual foreign friends and experiencing firsthand their traditions and culture.

In conclusion, apart from esoteric academic study, nothing can replace the experience of living in another country. Anyone fully committed to understanding the culture and language of another country must factor in a period of time in residence there.

text:

From my point of view, there should not be any restrictions or obligations to attend both face-to-face and online education systems. Individuals must be able to choose the one that they wish.

exam_question: Some people feel that equality between the genders has already been achieved while others feel there is considerable progress to be made. Discuss both views and give your own opinion
text:
Women say that men and women should be treated equally so we can attain gender equality

In terms of the law, females are now equal to males. They can vote in elections and stand for political office. In the early twentieth century, this was not the case and women had to fight for the right to cast their vote in elections. Furthermore, women have the same rights to own property as men. This was also not the case in the past.

Nevertheless, females suffer from indirect discrimination in many other ways. Statistically, females are still paid less on average than males. Although laws have been put in place to ensure equality of pay for the same job, men continue to dominate management positions while women are assigned administrative and support roles. Their average salary is lower as a result.

Furthermore, the burden of childcare falls more heavily on the mother than the father. Many companies are reluctant to female employees in their late twenties and early thirties for fear of the women becoming pregnant and placing the burden of paying maternity care on the shoulders of the company. This is something that is quantifiable and very difficult to expose.

Females have the same right to a career and to progress in that career as their male counterparts, but they are being denied this opportunity due to hidden discrimination at all levels in our community. Although the law has changed to uphold women’s rights, our community will remain unequal until these hidden forms of unfairness disappear, something that would require a sea change in attitudes on behalf of the general public.

exam_question: People are annoyed or entertained by advertising, but they are not affected by advertisements when making shopping decisions. To what extent you agree or disagree?
text:
Many believe that advertising does not influence actual buying decisions. In my opinion, though this may be true in the majority of instances, advertising is nonetheless extremely effective.

Those who feel that advertising serves little useful purpose can point to the most typical response from consumers. Whether they are on the internet, on television, or in real life, most individuals endeavour to skip or ignore ads. There are only isolated cases when a shopper will see an ad and as a direct result make a purchase. For example, YouTube advertisements have included a feature to “skip ads” that has become an automatic response from nearly every viewer. Even when forced to watch ads, such as in the cinema before a film starts, consumers are unlikely to remember the products or services and there is a strong chance they will take out their phones to completely shut out distracting commercials.

Nonetheless, advertisements have a limited yet powerful efficacy . The strongest evidence for this comes from the enduring health of the advertising industry. This flourishing  is because advertisements only need to yield results occasionally in order to be successful. For example, a fast food company such as McDonald’s or KFC might run an advertisement with the profitable expectation of only converting 1% of viewers, accepting the 99% failure rate as part of the business. Moreover, the 1% who make an immediate purchase is only one piece of the overall strategy. Advertising raises brand awareness and may lead to later consumption and even have a subliminal effect that is difficult to trace.

In conclusion, advertising is not designed to be effective at all times but instead to slowly influence and achieve the occasional success. In the aggregate, it is worthwhile for corporations to advertise even if the most common outcome is to be ignored.

 Gender equality is still a long way off and there are still some fields in which women are not thought of on an equal footing with men. exam_question: Some scientists believe that in the future computers will be more intelligent than human beings. While some see this as a positive development others worry about the negative consequences. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
text:
The advancement of technology has sparked a debate on whether computers can surpass human intelligence. While some scientists believe that this is a positive trend, others insist on considering possible negative impact. I would like to discover supporting ideas for each matter and mention my viewpoint.

People in science who embrace the idea of predominance of computer intelligence claim that the benefits of this evolving can outweigh any drawbacks. The more powerful computers are the more complex calculations can be done and, as a result, more breakthroughs can be achieved in science, technology, medicine, etc. In addition, computers can assist in more mundane or semi-mundane tasks and jobs and prevent human mistakes. Furthermore, this evolution looks safe as machines are limited to program scripts developed by humans, so their behaviour is limited by predefined rulesets. From my perspective, these arguments sound persuasive enough to join the team of supporters of this tendency.

From another point of view,  the consequences of computer improvement cannot be fully predicted. We should consider that this powerful technology can be weaponized by malicious individuals and be used in developing more lethal and sophisticated mass destruction weapons or  spreading more contagious computer viruses. Moreover, we should take into account unintentional human mistakes that can lead to life-threatening consequences. For instance, a flaw in medical software can cause invalid drug dosages and, as a result, death or life-lasting disabilities. However, these potential risks can be mitigated through legal and physical regulations.

Taking into consideration written above, we can conclude that ongoing debate around surpassing human intelligence by computers necessitates careful consideration of the benefits and risks involved. Striking a harmonious balance between improvement and regulations is crucial to ensure that we can harness positive outcomes while minimizing potential drawbacks.

exam_question: The best way to make the road transport of goods safer is to ask drivers to take a driving test each year. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Nevertheless, these days, many accidents occur not due to the driver’s inexperience, but due to the atrocious quality of roads: the presence of holes or slippery roads in winter. The local government should track the conditions of the roads in the same way that drivers should look after the state of their car. Every year more and more collisions are the result of vehicle’s malfunctioning. In addition to passing the annual exams, drivers should also take their car for a serviceability check every year.

To conclude, annual conducting and testing of drivers is a really positive development, but in order to reduce the number of traffic accidents to a minimum, local authorities should monitor the good condition of the roads, and drivers should take care of their car and do not forget to send it in for repair for inspection.

exam_question: Many government think that economic progress is their most important goal. Some people, hoever, think that others types of progress are equally important for a country. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion
text:

exam_question: Some believe that people should make efforts to fight climate change while others think it is better to learn to live with it. Discuss both views and give your own opinion

On the other hand, the effort still has a minor effect on the global temperature and it is increasingly important for people to adapt to the sudden change. Thus, people are able to secure their own lives to extend their longevity and promote their prosperity. 

In conclusion, I agree that people should take responsible acts to prevent the rise of temperature, which can gradually alter the current situation. However, the fast change of climate requires people to come up with a clever way to protect their own lives.

exam_question: In the past, knowledge was contained in books. Nowadays, knowledge is uploaded to the internet. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Despite the disadvantage impact on the Internet as the source of the learnings, there are obviously more essential benefits of using mostly websites for the needed information. exam_question: Nowadays, distance-learning programs have gained popularity, but some people argue that online courses can never be good as those taken at a college or university in person. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
Although face-to-face learning has been the traditional way of teaching for centuries, in recent years, online learning has become increasingly popular, and the trend is here to stay. However, few contend that on-campus courses are more effective in delivering education than distance learning. This essay completely disagrees with this view because online courses are far more flexible as well as allowing students to set the pace of the course. 

The two primary ways that make these online courses more flexible are because they are far more accessible and compelling. Firstly, students can easily access online materials at any time and from any location over the internet without having to attend face-to-face lectures. Moreover, a plethora of students are mainly attending on-campus lectures to take notes as passive learners, whereas distance learners are already motivated to study their material. Furthermore, working people often find it challenging to get time off work for face-to-face classes, and regardless of this mode’s benefits, they leave the course. For instance, many studies by Harvard have shown that retention rates for online learners are much higher than for traditional in-person students because it increases accessibility and removes physical limitations.  

Admittedly, many would agree that traditional teacher-led classes have many advantages, such as more interaction with like-minded students and teachers. While that may be true, to some extent, online programs give learners complete control over their learning so they can study at their own pace. Consequently, they can work quickly through areas they understand and spend more time on areas they do not. This would lead to better academic results, which is the overarching purpose of the course. As was seen in recent years, multinational firms such as Facebook and Google hired more of their workforce who studied through online schooling than those on campus.

In conclusion, this essay has supported the view that distance learning offers invaluable benefits for both scholars and educational institutions and is undoubtedly effective as face-to-face in delivering quality education. Online courses would also be essential if nations are to achieve their primary goal of educating all their citizens. Besides, in online learning, learners can decide what to dig more deeply into and spend more time learning due to the flexibility and self-paced nature of the course.

exam_question: People these days watch TV, films and other programmes alone rather than with other people. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages
text:
Nowadays, people often choose to watch TV, films, and other programs alone rather than with others. This trend increases personal freedom and enhances focus but also raises concerns about the loss of collective experiences. This essay will argue that despite some disadvantages, the benefits of watching entertainment alone outweigh the drawbacks. 

One significant advantage of watching movies alone is the freedom to choose the film genre. When watching with others, it can be challenging to find a movie that everyone agrees on. Watching alone eliminates this need for compromise, allowing individuals to select their preferred content. This personal freedom means viewers can enjoy their favourite genres without the need for negotiation, enhancing their viewing experience. Additionally, watching alone allows for deeper immersion in the content, leading to a better understanding and appreciation of the material. For instance, a romantic movie enthusiast can watch their favourite films without fear of judgment, which improves their focus and allows for critical analysis of the content. 

However, one notable disadvantage of watching TV and films alone is the loss of communal experience. Shared viewing often leads to discussions, shared laughter, and collective emotions, which can enhance the enjoyment of the content and strengthen social bonds. Without these shared experiences, individuals may miss out on opportunities to connect with others over common interests. To mitigate this, individuals can still engage in discussions about the films they've watched alone with friends and family, thereby combining the benefits of personal freedom with the advantages of social interaction.

In conclusion, while watching TV and films alone can lead to a loss of shared experiences, the benefits of increased personal freedom and enhanced focus are significant. Individuals can choose their preferred content and immerse themselves fully without distractions. Although this trend might reduce social interactions related to shared viewing experiences, discussing films later with friends and family can help bridge this gap. Overall, the advantages of watching entertainment alone outweigh the disadvantages.

exam_question: Some people say History Is one of the most important School subjects. Other people think that in today's world subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
text:
It is believed by some that history should be taught more in schools, while others argue that subjects like science and technology are more important due to the nature of our modern world. Both perspectives have their merits and the decision on which subject to prioritize should ultimately belong to the learner's preference.

On the one hand, understanding a country's origin and culture through history is crucial for fostering patriotism and providing valuable life lessons. Historical events reveal to young generations the immense sacrifices made by their ancestors to protect their country, enabling them to enjoy a peaceful present. By studying significant historical moments, students can learn to appreciate their current lives and avoid repeating past mistakes. This knowledge instils a sense of gratitude and respect for previous generations' sacrifices.

On the other hand, the rapid advancements in technology necessitate a strong foundation in science and technology to meet society's increasing demands for high-tech products and services. Students who lack familiarity with state-of-the-art technology may face challenges in professional settings, potentially leading to unemployment or inefficiency at work. In today's world, scientific and technological literacy is indispensable for career success and innovation.

However, the importance of history versus natural science subjects should be determined by the learners themselves, based on their future career directions and personal interests. Students should be taught the value of each subject and guided to invest more time in the one that aligns best with their academic strengths and career aspirations.

In conclusion, learning about the past fosters a love and knowledge for our homeland and provides valuable lessons, while scientific and technological subjects prepare us for the future workplace. Increasing learning time in a particular subject should be a personal choice rather than an imposition by external factors like schools.

exam_question: Many people put their personal information online (address, telephone number, and so on) for purposes such as signing up for social networks or online banking. Is this a positive or negative development?

On the other hand, I would disagree with this statement because it has exposed people to hacker threats. exam_question: The manufacturing and use of cars damages the environment but their popularity is increasing. Why is this? How could this be controlled?

exam_question: People these days watch TV, films and other programmes alone rather than with other people. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages.
text:
In contemporary times, numerous people prefer to watch TV, films, and other programmes alone rather than with their friends or families. This essay attempts to shed light on the merits and demerits of this tendency before concluding that the latter is more significant.

On the one hand, it is understandable why audiences intend to enjoy digital entertainment on their own. First and foremost, it could help them have an enjoyable life. For example, viewers could choose their favourite content without worrying about the opinions of others, which could put their minds at ease and recharge their energy after hard working shifts. Furthermore, being alone might enhance the quality of the watching experience. This is because it could allow the individuals to fully immerse themselves in the content, thus, they might understand more deeply as well as feel more delighted and satisfied.

On the other hand, there are a host of compelling reasons as to why I am convinced that audiences should share their leisure time with others. One rationale is that this decision could greatly improve people's relationships. To be more specific, spending time watching TV shows and broadcasts with members of the family means that the members can comprehend each other through the conversations and discussions among them. As a result, they could not only strengthen their ties but also get through the conflicts quickly. Another justification is that parents could protect their children against the negative effects of unsuitable content. In fact, there are various 18+ label movies on TV, and those could be easily accessed if there were no preventions or supervisors from their parents, thereby leading ineligible audiences to imitate bad behaviours such as toxicity, bullying, or racism.

In conclusion, while it is irrefutable that the loneliness in  television recreation might have some advantages, I would contend that the downsides overshadow the upsides.

exam_question: Some think the current generation should take steps to protect the environment for the next generation. To what extend do you agree or disagree.
text:
It’s a well known fact that humans have been polluting the environment for a long time. We can obviously feel it only in particular places of the globe, but most people around the world can’t really tell how vast the problem is. To find a real solution it’s important to keep in mind that there is no any specific company or person that could be considered accountable for ecological meltdown. The responsibility lies on every and each of us.

The internal combustion engine is to be thanked for numerous technological and economic advantages during past 150 years. Previous generations faced so many crises, that they had no choice, but to come up with more and more advanced technologies in order to catch up with the rest of the world. One of the most vivid examples probably would be events of World War 2. The most brilliant minds across the globe tried to surpass the enemy with new military inventions. No one at that time really thought about the consequences on environment or even political changes that the Manhattan Project, for example, could have brought. Everyone was focused mainly on two things: either defeating the enemy or discovering new ways of making profit out of new technologies. Or it could be both.

Now humanity has to carry this legacy of clueless capitalist mindset of the past. The modern world created by our ancestors is in urgent need for a global change. Unfortunately, few people realize that real steps must be made only with radical changes in the International Law system. Moreover, we need to revise our political and economic agendas. This is why it’s absolutely crucial to educate people on this problem, to talk about global warming in school and use media to spread awareness and inform people about how they can contribute. 

I am personally convinced that our generation is responsible for the future we will leave for our children to live in. Because right now the world is on the edge of a fatal catastrophe, and it’s our direct responsibility to take some actions. Everyone can contribute, but it’s not enough if governments do not rewrite and adapt new laws. Updating legislation to the current situation might take a considerable amount of time, so this is why we have to hurry up. In the end, there is no one else who will do it instead of us.

exam_question: Some today argue that schools are no longer necessary because children can learn so much from the internet and be educated at home. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
There are some today who would argue that the internet has sufficiently supplanted the role of traditional education so as to make it redundant. In my opinion, though the internet opens up possibilities for learning, schools are a crucial filter.

What separates the internet from how other advances in technology have impacted education is greater accessibility to information. It is no exaggeration to claim that nearly everything can be found on the internet. School age children can access educational videos on YouTube, read online articles and use interactive learning platforms. As they get older, the possibilities expand and include scholarly articles, video-conferencing platforms like Zoom, and online newspapers from every country in the world that can be translated to your native language in modern internet browsers. There is immense potential for auto-didacts and parents who choose to homeschool.

Nonetheless, schools are the real world editors of the internet. A lot of news is thrown up instantly and not carefully vetted. This means that students can get led into dark corners such as alt-left and right websites that specialise in sensationalised propaganda. Children and teens are especially susceptible to what they read online as they might be less skeptical. Teachers have more life experience and their training helps them approach information critically. They can then pass these skills on to their pupils by teaching them how to read closely, spot biases, and check information through a number of primary and secondary sources. Without teachers, students are more likely to be indoctrinated rather than educated.

In conclusion, teachers are important to dispel the inherent risks of unreliable online information. Schools and administrators ought to take a long-view in order to assess the value of the internet for learning.

  In conclusion, although social networking sites offer benefits, they have a significant negative impact on both individuals and society. exam_question: When cars and cyclists use the same roads, there are often problems. Why is this the case? What are the solutions?
text:
Nowadays different ways of transportation are expanding, while the roads remained the same. As a result, various kinds of vehicles use the same road simultaneously which would be to some extent problematic. Although there are specific root causes behind this concern, effective policies such as expanding roads and considering cycling culture can be adapted to remedy the situation. 

There are two main reasons why sharing the same road can cause serious problems both for car  drivers and cyclists. Firstly, due to the different size and qualities and safety, criteria there would be different rules associated with each of these. To put it another way, the speed limit belonging to the cycles would definitely be a distraction for car drivers who are moving faster in a safer vehicle. Secondly, car drivers are in a solid cabin which protects them from serious injuries in contrast to the riders who are exposed to hurt seriously in case of accidents. In addition, one of the very important advantages of having a child late is mental preparedness and financial stability which helps both parents to be able to cater for their basic needs after birth. when both parents are mentally prepared, they tend to have peace of mind and also cater for themselves, forming intimacy together. For example, in a survey conducted by World Health Organization(WHO), it was published that women that gave birth late in Nigeria are more responsible and care for their children more than others. Afterwards, women that gave birth at an early age abandon their children  due to insufficient income and lack of mental preparedness which affect their children's education and mental well-being . Therefore, waiting till old age before having a child is better.

In summary, despite the several complications that follow giving birth at an advanced age, the merits outweigh its demerits as both couples would be more prepared mentally and financially.

Moreover, companies should implement the alternative of buying items in a more environmentally friendly approach. For instance, Unilever sells their refill detergent at the supermarket, by refilling the old container or people can bring their bottles.

In conclusion, the destruction of the environment caused by increasing goods consumption is mainly caused by the growing number of waste and insufficient recycling factories’ capacity. On the one hand, supporters of teaching religion in schools argue that religious education plays a role in shaping students' ethical behavior. On the other hand, those who hold an opposing view argue that it would not be logical to teach every child the same religion, especially in countries with diverse backgrounds. Currently, parents enroll their children in top-performing schools based on qualifying exams which pave the way for university admission and career pursuits. For instance, studying Buddhism may have no impact on someone's career choice of becoming an engineer; therefore, it should not be included in institutions.

In conclusion, while teaching religion can offer benefits such as promoting ethical behavior among students and providing knowledge of different faiths, these advantages are outweighed by its inefficiency and potential divisive nature. exam_question: Many think that religion should be taught in schools while others think it should be avoided. Discuss both sides and give your own opinion.
text:
Religion has always been a topic of controversy when it comes to its place in educational institutions. Some argue that religion should be taught in schools as a way to educate students about morality, ethics, and cultural traditions. Others believe that schools should avoid teaching religion altogether in order to maintain a secular and impartial atmosphere. 

Those in favour of teaching religion in schools believe that it can provide a solid foundation for ethical and moral development in students. Religion can serve as a source of guidance on how to navigate moral dilemmas and live an ethical life. It can also serve as an opportunity for students to learn about different cultural practices and values, developing empathy and understanding.

On the other hand, those opposed to teaching religion in schools argue that it opens the door for bias and discrimination against certain religions. When a particular religion is taught in school, students may feel forced to conform to the teachings and beliefs of that specific religion, potentially alienating students of different faiths or those who don't believe in religion at all. Additionally, it may be challenging for schools to appropriately represent a wide range of religions and cultures in a way that is respectful and comprehensive.

In my opinion, the best approach is an educational approach that is inclusive of all religions and, at the same time, neutral. Rather than promoting a specific religion, schools can teach world religions in a comparative manner, with a focus on history and culture, without endorsing or discouraging any specific belief system. This method provides an opportunity for students to understand and respect different religions and beliefs rather than feeling forced to conform to one particular set of beliefs.

In conclusion, whether should religion be taught in schools is a sensitive issue that requires careful consideration. While some may argue for outright avoidance or for full support, the optimal path lies in a middle ground that allows for a comprehensive and neutral approach to religious education.

exam_question: After graduation, many students take a year to travel. Some think that it would be more useful to work for a year. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:

In my opinion, it is much better to develop your capacity for leisure activity rather than get a job in this interim period.

The main reason many advocate employment during a gap year is the cultivation of a strong work ethic. When someone begins working, their bad habits necessarily subside. For example, a worker has to be on time, work diligently, follow orders, get along with co-workers, show initiative, have a positive attitude, endure long days, and make ends meet with little pay. This is the molding process of adulthood which entails reconciling your desires with the community's expectations at large. The individual who opts to spend their gap year working will enter university more well-rounded, disciplined, and humble.

However, a strong work ethic is bound to develop later, while the ability to enjoy one’s leisure while traveling is a far more valuable skill. Most people acclimate to working with a part-time job during high school or academy. At worst, they develop these qualities after graduation. Since they have been either working or studying their entire lives they have neglected the ability to enjoy the leisure that distinguishes higher classes. The average person who has been working their entire life goes on holiday or retires and feels restless. To enjoy your leisure time traveling, you must be able to set aside future worries, live in the moment, get outside your comfort zone, have a wide range of hobbies and skills, and be active for a full day without a workday. Chances to cultivate these habits will see far less light with a career and family, so it is best to nourish them before university.

In conclusion, the gap year is a crucial space for individuals to develop personal relationships in their leisure time. This is important as an ever-advancing career can become an undesirable transformational experience.

exam_question: The best way to make the road transport of goods safer is to ask drivers to take a driving test each year. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
In the modern world, it is undeniable that ensuring the safety of road transport for goods has become a major concern in many countries. Some people argue that the best way to improve safety is to require drivers to take a driving test every year. Although some agree with this view, I am opposed to it due to several reasons, which will be examined in this essay.

One of the most apparent reasons is that annual driving tests alone may not address the main causes of accidents in goods transport. To illustrate, many road incidents result from factors such as driver fatigue, poor vehicle maintenance, or unsafe road conditions rather than a lack of driving ability. For instance, even experienced drivers who pass regular tests may still be involved in accidents if they are required to work long hours or operate poorly maintained vehicles, suggesting that testing alone cannot guarantee safety.

Another point that should not be overlooked is that broader measures could be more effective in improving transport safety. To clarify, stricter regulations on working hours, regular vehicle inspections, and the use of modern safety technology may have a greater impact. For example, installing monitoring systems that track driver behaviour and vehicle performance can help prevent dangerous situations before they occur. Such approaches focus on the overall transport system rather than solely on individual drivers.

To recapitulate, it is evident that although annual driving tests might help maintain driver competence, they do not address the wider causes of transport accidents. Therefore, I believe that requiring yearly tests is not the best solution, and governments should instead adopt comprehensive safety policies that include regulation, technology, and proper working conditions for drivers.

exam_question: Climate change is a phenomenon that affects countries all over the world. Many people strongly believe that it is the responsibility of individuals, rather than corporations and governments, to deal with this problem. To what extent do you agree?
text:
In recent years, global warming has been receiving a great deal of media attention around the world due to its substantial impacts on human life. Although individuals have to take the responsibility to cope with climate change, I agree that corporations and governments always play a key role because of their greater responsibility and capacity. 

There are a number of reasons why corporations and governments could tackle climate change better than individuals who do not have enough power and capacity to make changes worldwide. First, governments have the ability to affect large systematic change for global warming by enacting  legislation requiring both locals and corporations to abide by certain restrictions. For example, governments introduce laws for corporations to reduce and recycle effective waste before sending them to the environment, which climate change can be seriously countered. Second, corporations, especially in the manufacturing and mining industries, should support financially to cope with the increasing temperature in the world as they are operating for business and directly contributing to climate change. Therefore, it can be implied that if corporations were not held accountable for their contribution to global warming, the issue of climate change would inevitably be exacerbated.

On the other hand, individuals could support compacting climate change correlating with the governments, however, they could only deal with local and personal problems. The inhabitants do not have the rights to issue policies or laws to make great impacts worldwide, so they can do small things for their communities. For instance, people follow strict orders from the government, such as walking or taking public transportation rather than using private vehicles in order to reduce traffic congestion, travel time, air pollution and energy consumption which increase climate change. In addition, people should have to worry about personal problems as well as living costs, so they would focus on their life first before protecting the environment on a large scale. It should be noticed that governments have many responsibilities to tackle global warming, which is part of the basic security towards their citizens to make the world a better place. 

In conclusion, actively combating global warming must be regarded as top priority given the highest urgency. Governments and corporations worldwide should take steps to ensure that climate change remains at bay rather than individuals.

exam_question: There are severe social consequences to housing shortages in cities and only the government can solve these problems.To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
In modern-day society, there is a common conception that social drawbacks coming from the lack of housing in cities can only be tackled by the government. As far as this argument goes, I am not in favour of the idea for the following reasons. 

First and foremost, this phenomenon can be solved due to the contribution of citizens. It can be clearly seen that inhabitants can devote their properties to social housing plans, laying the foundation for them to be implemented. For instance, thanks to residents’ support towards the trend of dedicating private estate, it is estimated that the proportion of the homeless in my neighbourhood shrank remarkably by five per cent in the course of 10 years, starting from 2010. Another pivotal remedy is contributing to charity funds, which are launched to assist homeless people. As an example, thanks to those funds, the number of cheap shelters in my backyard is estimated to skyrocket from nearly 100 in 2010 to about 2000 in 2020, lifting a large number of people out of homelessness. In short, the assistance of dwellers is beneficial, but it is not enough to deal with the problem. 

Furthermore, this part of the essay depicts several therapies the government can put forward to tackle this issue. First, the investment in social housing is a noteworthy solution. Apparently, by building more social houses can people have more opportunities to acquire their homes, leading to the plunging ratio of slums and shanty towns, giving the poor chances to have better lives. Moreover, the authority can offer incentives and subsidies to real estate developers. For instance, the chairman of my city reduced taxes for entrepreneurs who could build vertical buildings as a way to tackle the lack of shelters. 

In a nutshell, I pen down by reconfirming that I do not support the idea claiming that the consequences of the shortage of accommodations can only be solved by the government. Nevertheless, the issue can be tackled due to the contribution of both citizens and the authority.

exam_question: Some today argue that schools are no longer necessary because children can learn so much from the internet and be educated at home. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
By the advent of the internet and its spread among almost all humans, numerous information resources have become reachable for people, among which the educational contents are no exception. However, I argue that this valuable amenity can not be completely substituted by conventional schools, because some advantages of physical classes are not available on the internet.

On the one hand, it is obvious that the internet has revolutionized the education system. For example, the online courses have removed the time and location barrier and made it possible for people who live in far-flung and developing areas to attend online classes, which in turn helps eliminate illiteracy around the world. Additionally, A variety of articles, photos, videos and materials are shared publicly on the internet so that every pupil can access them, download them, and review them as many times as they need thanks to the features of the internet.

Nevertheless, I opine that the conventional classes are irreplaceable because they bring about some benefits that are not provided by the internet. For instance, children would experience peer interaction with their classmates as well as learning to compete with their peers, join teamwork groups and ask for help or give help to their counterparts. Furthermore, by attending group classes, adolescents learn how to abide by the rules and respect the authorities. Likewise, traditional classes provide monitoring and evaluation for teachers to assure students are on the right track.

To summarize, although the internet could bring about plenty of useful facilities for educating children, it can not be completely replaced by schools, because it lacks a number of considerable options of schools. It is better to use it as a supplement for studies under the supervision of teachers.

exam_question: Some people think that social networking sites have a huge negative impact on both individuals and society. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
In the contemporary world, social media have been involved in everyone's life. Most people claim that they could not live without social networking websites, however, I believe that social media such as Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter, actually have enormous negative impacts on both individuals and society as a whole.

There is no doubt that social applications on our mobile phones or iPad provide us with numerous benefits. For example, we are able to chat with our family members and old friends even if they are living in other countries, which strengthens the connections between people living far away from each other. In addition, by following the accounts of celebrities, we can know their daily lives and even communicate with them.

Nevertheless, being addicted to social media can negatively affect people, especially youngsters. Firstly, young adults are typically occupied by a large number of school assignments, but social media can easily distract them, leading to the waste of their available time. Moreover, spending several hours a day texting friends or checking famous people's most recent posts is an unhealthy lifestyle, which can contribute to obesity and other diseases.

Furthermore, social media can have adverse effects on society as well. If most young adults are addicted to social media, they would have much worse performance both in schools and at work, resulting in a potential decrease in talented youngsters, and the economy of the country can also be negatively affected. Additionally, social media are filled with fake news. If a significant amount of people were misled by that unreal news, they would vote for the wrong candidate in the election, resulting in damage to the democratic system.

In conclusion, while social media can bring us joyful and fulfilling lives, I firmly believe that they have considerable negative effects on both individuals and society.

exam_question: Some think that it is more important for children to engage in outdoor activities instead of playing videogames. To what extent to you agree or disagree?

For example, according to one statistics of The U.S. Department of Health, 1 out of 3 children in the United States is overweight or obese as a consequence of staying at home playing video games and don’t get enough activity, while youngsters who spend time outdoors are 49% less prone to health problems. 

Secondly, outdoor games in the company of peers are useful for developing communication skills. Furthermore, offline dialogues are incredibly important for the ability to express emotions in words and to understand the feeling of others, since online communication is limited to short phrases and emojis and does not convey the beauty of real communication. For instance, according to psychologists, adolescents who are not involved in outdoor plays in 8 out of 10 cases have difficulty building friendly relations with classmates because in the establishment of relations of real life is much more complex than 2 clicks and 4 emojis online.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that participation in active games with peers in playgrounds and parks will lead to improving socialization skills schoolchildren, and also increase physical health.

exam_question: Some people argue job satisfaction is more important that job security. Others believe a permanent job is more important. Discuss both views and give your own opinions.
text:

In this essay, both the views will be critiqued before reaching a reasoned conclusion.

On the one hand, job satisfaction plays a more important role due to its permanent working environment. In the modern days, people easily get stressed by deadlines and extra shifts, which is not surprising to comprehend that the unemployment rate has risen significantly. To put it simply, employees give up their current job because they cannot feel comfortably treated, thus keeping hunting for the comfort in their occupation. Moreover, in order to balance between personal life and career, as well as reaching happiness, a free-stress job would be the optimum for those workers. 

Conversely, working consistently in one position is considered to be more vital, since it will provide not only a stable income for the employees, but also a permanent working environment. To be more precise, job security might guarantee the stability of the workers’ job position as well as preventing from being unemployed. Furthermore, being satisfactory when working can be a hurdle in getting promoted. An illustration for this is when the staffs decide not to do much of their tasks so as to have more time for relaxation, they will firmly stay in the low job position of the company. 

In conclusion, despite the idea that people should choose job satisfaction rather than preserve their occupation by being stable in only one organization. To my mind, it depends on each person’s circumstance to decide which advice will do them good, as long as they find it convenient.

exam_question: Some people believe that the government should spend more money putting in more works of art like paintings and statues in cities to make them better places to live in. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
Many people agree that local governments have their responsibilities of investing money in creating more works of art like painting and statues in cities in order to provide a comfortable, picturesque living environment. However, I opine that local governments should use their annual budgets more wisely and invest in essential sectors such as education system, health care service and pollution prevention instead of in arts.

Firstly, more arts in public around the cities may lead urban views more beautiful and attractive while it is not a necessary element to maintain the high quality of life for local residents. As comparing to increasing budgets in art creations to create stunning street views, other strategies such as constructing more local roads to reduce traffic jams, planting more trees along the roads, especially in inner cities, and hiring more cleaning workers to keep streets clean are more important and efficient in providing lovely and well-organized urban living habitats for local residents to enjoy their lives. 

In addition, arts provide a sense of beauty for their audiences, but they are not essential for residents' daily life. Although modern arts may enhance urban views and create some unique features for local cultures, well-organized and well-funded health care service and excellent educational institutes play a crucial role in residents' daily life. People can live without arts in cities while social services are definitely disturbed by the lack of proper and well-operating schools or hospitals. Hence, investing limited annual budgets in creating arts across the cities is not a wise strategy whereas spending money on fundamental facilities is a key step to create a better living environment for local residents.

Finally, the majority of residents commonly strive for a city with clean air and close-zero pollution to raise their families instead of seeking modern arts. Thus, eliminating and preventing all kinds of pollutions is a key point for local governments to make their cities more environmentally friendly and attractive. Clean air, abundant trees and well-organized residential communities are more significant for residents' daily life than arts. Unless a city is extremely wealthy with high annual revenue, the annual budget should not be used in creating arts to make a better living environment. However, only a small proportion of the annual budget on arts may be acceptable. 

In conclusion, financial budgets for local governments are limited. Arts may enhance the beauty of a city, but a lean living environment with low pollution, well-organized public facilities such as hospitals and schools, and well-developed civil blueprints are more crucial to provide a better living condition for local residents. Therefore, it is unwise to invest money in creating arts to decorate the city.

exam_question: Developing the economy will always damage the environment. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
It is argued that the economic growth always leads detrimental effect on our natural habitat.  While it has been generally true for the last two or three centuries, the emergence of sustainable development has changed the game. The previous growth model involves relentless exploitation of the natural resources. Today's approach, on the other hand, facilitates the means and tools to preserve the Earth.

From early years of the "Industrial Revolution" up to 50 years ago, humans have proudly, and yet naively, consumed natural resources and polluted the Earth. Early engineers and thinkers believed that the planet is so vast that it can easily absorb our polluting leftovers. Although it is true in a small scale, it has shown the opposite for mass production. Humans' activities have polluted clean water resources, air, and the Earth soil, in exchange for more profit. For instance, the production of jean trousers consumes thousands of gallons of clean water and produces the same amount of sewage, which is poured back to the flow. So, in the old definition of development, more production means more deterioration. 

As humans got aware about their actions' outcome, they changed their growth model into a sustainable one. A sustainable model facilitates means, protocols, and tools to minimize threats to the environment, and simultaneously the maintaining the production. Take textile industry as an example. The new methods of producing materials and processes, which consumes much less water and produces much less sewage, are the engineers and scientist endeavor and contribution to preserve the nature. Although many sustainable processes are harder to implement or more expensive, a growing number of companies are embracing them. So, I believe that as we are going forward in the history, economic growth is getting less equivalent to damage to the nature.

To conclude, it is essential to understand that which model of progress are we discussing about. The former model of development has constantly exploited and destructed the environment, while the contemporary notion of development tries to preserve the Earth.

exam_question: There are severe social consequences to housing shortages in cities and only the government can solve this problem. To what extent do you agree or disagree
