exam_question: Many researchers believe that we can now study the behaviour of children to see if they will grow up to be criminals, while others disagree. To what extent do you think crime is determined by genetics? Is it possible to stop children from growing up to be criminals?
text:
There are many psychologists today who believe that crime comes from inborn, genetic characteristics. In my opinion, genetics play a small role in criminal behaviour and it is much more sensible to combat crime by looking to family circumstances.

 

Those who believe strongly in the role of genetics in determining future behaviour can point to case examples and hard data. It is very common for the children of violent criminals to display some degree of abnormal behaviour as children and later in life. Scientists can ground their theories of crime by mapping the genetic code of an individual and then identifying similarities between the family members of criminals. However, their results may uncover some genetic factors but it is much more likely that a child raised by a criminal will simply have a poor upbringing and social factors will explain their anti-social behaviour. This is supported by recent research into developmental psychology showing the physical changes that occur in brain formation as a result of upbringing.

Therefore, it is largely possible to prevent most crime by taking an active, positive role in childcare. A good counter-example of this comes from the case studies of serials killers. Without exception, all serial killers came from abusive, broken homes. The physical and sexual abuse present in their childhood, later manifested itself in their compulsions to exert power over others. Naturally, this does not mean that abuse necessarily leads to crime, as many others overcome their difficult backgrounds to become well-adjusted adults. It does, however, imply a large proportion of criminal behaviour can be prevented by a supportive family environment. Knowing that they are loved and accepted by their parents, will make children less likely to seek attention through bad behaviour or abuse drugs to cope with their problems, both of which are early indicators of possible criminality.

In conclusion, though nature may be a marginal factor in criminal psychology, I believe that emphasis on the social environment is the real key to fighting crime. It is therefore important to invest in social services, education, and child welfare programs.

exam_question: Developing the economy will always damage the environment. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

exam_question: It is now possible for scientists and tourists to travel to remote natural environment, such as the South Pole. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

exam_question: Some feel that countries should produce most of the food that is eaten in their country and import as little as possible. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
Many today are increasingly of the opinion that countries should be self-sufficient in their food production and import as little as possible. Though I grant this is unrealistic in certain countries, the economic implications are convincing.

In most countries, imported foods are simply a luxury, but this belies those nations where imports ensure survival. Some of these countries include populous Southeast Asian nations, and numerous Middle Eastern and African countries. The reasons range from poorly developed infrastructure, little arable soil, and increased vulnerability to natural disasters. Many Asian countries in particular, import and stockpile basic foods such as rice for potential catastrophes. As agricultural technology develops and allows for crops that require less water, their desperation will lessen but it would be inhumane today to starve citizens in these countries.

The above-mentioned scenarios are exceptions; the majority of countries would be better served through vibrant food cultivation and production industries. The economic impact is twofold. First, these industries employ thousands of agricultural and meatpacking workers. Secondly, these workers then contribute to the local economy by buying goods and services. Replace them with international food conglomerates and suddenly they are funding the GDP of another country. A good counterexample to this would be in South Korea, where the vast majority of products are nationally produced and, in fact, were some of the initial, primary sources of income for technology giants like Samsung and LG.

In conclusion, except in extreme cases, countries should import fewer food products to better serve their citizenry economically. There will always be a place for a limited range of imports, but it should not supersede local production.

exam_question: In the past, knowledge was contained in books. Nowadays, knowledge is uploaded to the internet. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

One major advantage of sharing knowledge on websites is that it is much cheaper and easier to access. Thus, uploading information online might help the knowledge to reach more audiences in a timely manner. To conclude, both books and the Internet have some advantages and disadvantages. While the Internet helps to deliver information quicker and cheaper, content on books seem to be verified. However, in the case of knowledge transfer, it is clear that books have more merits because the content has more credibility.

exam_question: Some people believe that it is good idea to share as much information as possible in scientific research, business and the academic world. Others believe that some information is too important or too valued to be shared freely. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
text:
In the contemporary era, the debate over the extent to which information should be shared in scientific research, business, and academia is fervent. While some advocate for the utmost transparency, others argue for the protection of certain valuable information. This essay will explore both perspectives before concluding with my stance on the matter.

Proponents of open information sharing contend that it is a catalyst for innovation. By disseminating research findings and methodologies, the scientific community can build upon existing knowledge, thereby accelerating the pace of discovery. Furthermore, the free flow of information can enhance efficiency by eliminating the redundancy of research efforts. Additionally, open collaboration fosters a global exchange of ideas, which is particularly crucial in addressing complex, cross-disciplinary challenges.

Conversely, critics warn of the potential risks associated with indiscriminate information sharing. Intellectual property rights are a primary concern, as the unrestricted dissemination of proprietary information can undermine the financial incentives for innovation. Moreover, there are legitimate security concerns, especially in sensitive fields such as biotechnology and defense, where the release of certain data could pose significant threats. Lastly, the sheer volume of shared information can lead to information overload, overwhelming individuals and impeding the absorption of truly valuable insights.

Striking a balance between the benefits and drawbacks of information sharing is essential. Policymakers and stakeholders must establish robust frameworks that safeguard intellectual property while encouraging the sharing of non-sensitive information. Trust mechanisms and authentication systems could be employed to ensure that information is shared responsibly and securely.

In conclusion, the question of how much information should be shared is not one-size-fits-all. The scientific and academic realms stand to gain immensely from an open exchange of ideas, which can lead to groundbreaking discoveries and advancements. However, in the business sector, particularly when it involves trade secrets, a more cautious approach is warranted. Ultimately, the goal should be to create an environment that fosters innovation and collaboration while safeguarding the rights and interests of individuals and organizations.

exam_question: Global warming is not caused by human activity. Changes in average temperatures throughout all climate zones are a normal phenomenon. Therefore, countries need not take any actions to combat global warming that would negatively impact their economies. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
text:
The debate over the causes of global warming has been ongoing for decades. While some argue that fluctuations in climate patterns are part of a natural cycle, others believe that human activity is the primary driver of rising global temperatures. In my opinion, despite the existence of natural climate variation, there is overwhelming scientific evidence that human actions, particularly the burning of fossil fuels, are significantly accelerating planetary warming. Therefore, countries must act, even if economic costs are involved.

Human activities, especially with the industrialisation and globalisation, have dramatically increased the concentration of greenhouse gas in the atmosphere. The scientific report of the EEA (European Environmental Agency) attributed the majority of recent temperature rises to the last 20 years industrial emissions. The burning of coal, oil and gas for energy, along with deforestation has intensified the greenhouse effect, leading to higher temperatures, loss of biodiversity, melting of polar ice caps, and more frequent extreme weather phenomena. Ignoring this human footprint would means disregarding decas of scientific evidences and consensus.

Although economic concers are valid, inaction on climate change may lead to even greater financial and humanitarian costs in the long term. Rising sea levels threaten coastal cities, and climate-related disasters can devastate agricolture, infractructure, and public health systems provoking a fall in economic revenues. Furthermore, investinf in renewable energy and sustainable technologies could stimulate new industries and create jobs, reducing short-term economic drawbacks. Thus, taking action against global warming is not only environmentally responsible but also economically strategic. 

In conclusion, while natural cycles are supposed to exist, human activity have accelerated the process. Dismissing the need for intervention only to protect economic interests is both short-sighted and dangerous but also selfish. Proactive climate policies are essential for ensuring a sustainable future and the further development of societies.

Firstly, many people argue that History is the most important in school curriculum. They believe History enables students to get familiar with their past, the historical happening belonging to them and the goals set by their forefathers. Moreover, they can also take the lessons from their previous happenings. In this way, they can contribute towards the progressive developments of their countries. Therefore, some people believe History is the most crucial subject.

On the other hand, many people assert that teaching Science and Technology are more in demand than History. They key reason for this stance can be the modern competitive world, where new developments and wonders in Science and Technology are occurring every moment. Each sector of this universe from needle to space missions is on the technologically rise. Therefore, if the students are not taught to excel in Science and Technology, they obviously can’t compete with rest of the world. For instance, in this world, my country can’t challenge the globe in the field of Science and technology as we have not focused on these evolving subjects. That’s why Science and technology are the most important in comparison to History.

To conclude, there are competing views on the importance of History vs science and Technology. In my opinion, despite History is considered a top school subject yet Science and technology are the top-most school curriculum to excel in this era by competing the rest of the world

exam_question: some people think that newly built houses should follow the style of old houses in local areas. Others think that people should have freedom to build houses of their own styles. Discuss both views and give your own opinions.
text:

On the one hand, it is compelling as to why there is a trend to preserve and continue old house design in local areas. The reason for this tendency is believed that citizens have a desire to protect traditional customs and patterns. To be more specific, old house constructions represent previous traditions that are considered to be historical, beautiful and extremely meaningful. Thus, it is really valuable to have more and more protection for them, not only for the purposes of national pride but also for education and tourism. For instance, a plethora of long-lasting buildings or streets in Hanoi city is now interestingly becoming hot tourist attractions for numerous foreigners and sources of materials for various students. 

On the other hand, I am strongly persuaded by the view that building accommodations in a free and personal way are still the optimal choice. exam_question: Many people put their personal information online (address, telephone number, and so on) for purposes such as signing up for social networks or online banking. Is this a positive or negative development?
text:
Many websites and online services like banking asking  people to use their personal information in the signing up process. I consider this as a negative development because it paves the way for potential damaging personal security breaches; moreover, it is unlikely for anyone to succeed in removing all of his data once they are uploaded online. 

Namely, putting personal information online exposes the individual to different sort of potential online crimes. For example, identity theft is becoming a nightmare now for banks and individuals, because of the sheer number of incidents happening daily. It begins with a hacker steals someone's private information to access his bank account, and withdraw the money or use it for online shopping. Usually, the victim contacts his bank to stop the transactions but it takes a long time and lots of efforts to prove to the bank the scheme. Hence, sometimes, the victim loses his assets indefinitely. Needless to say that many measures have been taken by banks and online security companies to counter these crimes, but it is an ongoing war with no winner yet. Therefore, it is a huge risk to use personal information in any online activity.

A second threat is that once the information is online there is no way to erase it completely. In other words, the digital records of any website are saved on multiple servers and on different search engines too, which makes it impossible to delete all the copies of the data. While the account holder may delete his account and leave the internet for good, all of his data are still online and can be found by an eager criminal. As a result, there is a permanent fear of being hacked despite all the steps taken to clear the web from any personal footprint. 

To conclude, using personal data online is a negative development because it exposes individuals to online crimes such as identity theft, and since the information will be always online, anyone is in a state of  constant threat to safety.

exam_question: Living in a country where you have to speak a foreign language can cause serious social problems as well practical problems. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement.
text:
People who live in a foreign country often have difficulties speaking foreign languages which might cause social and practical problems. I completely agree because having a language barrier while living in a foreign country might make our daily activities difficult.

Many people decide to live in foreign countries because the job or academic opportunities are promising. The biggest challenge that people will experience while living in a foreign country is the language barrier, especially when English is not their native language. Without preparation, people might experience difficulties in communicating with others, which could affect their daily activities.

For example, people who cannot speak the local language might experience difficulties in making friends. In addition, it might develop loneliness which most   people who live in foreign country experience. On the other hand, this feeling of loneliness combined with homesickness might affect their mental health. Therefore, it is important to learn a foreign language before deciding to live in a foreign country.

In conclusion, I think having language barriers while living in a foreign country could cause a serious problem which eventually could affect mental health. However, it could be prevented if we are prepared to learn the local language to communicate with the people.

exam_question: More and more people no longer read newspapers or watch TV programmes to get their news and instead read online. Is this a positive or negative development?
text:
Nowadays, many people are familiar with reading on the Internet as an alternative to reading tidings or watching TV shows to update their news and knowledge. From my point of view, I reckon that this is an advantageous development for some reasons mentioned in this essay.

On the one hand, there are a few drawbacks to reading online. Firstly, many fake and untruthful information is floating online. The Internet is a place where people can post anything they want. Therefore, there is plenty of unverified information and it has a bad impact on readers. Secondly, people can easily lose concentration on reading. If readers do not turn on “do not disturb” mode while reading, they can be affected by notifications from many applications or advertisements on the website and their reading experience will be interrupted. Thirdly, their health will also be influenced. Spending too much time on screen can lead to many health issues such as short-eye sighted state, and neck and back problems. 

On the other hand, reading online brings many benefits to readers. First and foremost, users can access data quickly and conveniently. They only need digital devices with an internet connection to be able to surf the web. Secondly, viewing online tidings helps save money. Most digital bulletin websites provide viewers with free information which helps them not have to pay money to buy printed newspapers. Last but not least, it contributes to environmental protection. Accessing digital info means that the use of paper to make newspapers is reduced  and the energy used for printing will also be decreased.

In conclusion, I hold a firm belief that reading online on the website is more beneficial than its drawbacks and this is a positive development. The importance is that each individual must know how to use it for the right purpose so that reading online will be effective

exam_question: Some people argue that job satisfaction is more important than job security, while others believe that they cannot always expect job satisfaction, and a permanent job is more important. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
text:
In modern society, there is no longer the attitude that “a job is for life”. Nowadays, many people take the option to change jobs while others prefer not to. . In this essay, I will discuss the viewpoints of both supporters and opponents, as well as give my own opinion.

On the one hand, a few people prefer to do the same business for the same company for the following two reasons. One of the main benefits of staying in one job is security. Changing work often means a period of instability, where one may have to think about moving house or temporarily losing a steady source of income. Thus, staying in one job means these problems are avoided. Another benefit of not changing occupation is that one is able to gain a lot of experience and expertise in his specific field. 

On the other hand, there are arguments in charge of changing jobs frequently. First of all, working in several different jobs often means that an individual/employee has more skill because people are seen as more dynamic and versatile. Secondly, from my own experience, I got bored when I spent too much time in a job. Following this, the quality of my work would suffer. Therefore, another benefit of changing works regularly is that people never get stuck in a rut. Besides, increased wages and promotion are usually easier to attain by changing jobs.

All in all, it can be said that the disadvantages of changing jobs are the advantages of staying put and vice versa. As I see it, changing jobs every once in a while is a bit more beneficial.

exam_question: Many governments think that economic progress is their most important goal. Some people, however, think that other types of progress are equally important for a country. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
text:
Economic development is, for most governments, the greatest goal of all. Other people believe that progress in health and education are as important. In this essay, I will discuss both views and explain why these three types of progress are equally essential for every country.   

On the one hand, it is thought by many that economic progress is the most important goal because it is how the development of a country is measured. For example, the difference between first world and third world countries is essentially the money produced by them. Another reason is that money makes people happier, less stressed and consequently, less mad at politicians. For instance, wealthy people do not complain about anything as they are satisfied with the life they carry, therefore if there is economic development there will not be so many protest rallies on the streets. 

On the other hand, some think that health is an important determinant of a country's level of development. India, in like manner, has a worse quality of life than Argentina because of the larger amount of preventable diseases they suffer such as diarrhoea. If people are ill and have to take medicines daily and require special care, the quality of life is noticeably reduced.  Another important type of progress is in education. The proportion of professionals in a country is thought to be an essential measure of its development. For instance, places where best universities are located, are known for their excellence and the quality workers they produce.

In conclusion, while some politicians consider that economic progress in their country is the most important goal, in my opinion, development in health and in education has been and should be just as essential. Adequate living conditions are ensured not only by money, but also by good sanitary measures and learning institutions. Therefore, this should always be taken into account when deciding on what measures to apply.

exam_question: It is now possible for scientists and tourists to travel to remote natural environments, such as South Pole. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
text:
With the advancement of technology and transportation, it has become possible for people to travel to remote natural environments, such as the South Pole. While some people worry that this trend can bring harm to fragile ecosystems, others see it as an opportunity for scientific progress and unique travel experiences. 

The ability to travel to remote natural areas provides clear benefits. For scientists, access to places like Antarctica is crucial for conducting research on climate change, ecosystems, and wildlife. Although, studies can deepen people’s understanding of global environmental problems and help governments create more effective conservation policies. For tourists, visiting pristine landscapes offers unique educational experiences that can raise awareness about the importance of protecting fragile environments. Moreover, tourism can generate funding for conservation projects and provide economic benefits to regions that support these expeditions. 

On the other hand, there are significant drawbacks. Increased human  activity in delicate ecosystems can cause irreversible damage. For example, waste, pollution, and disturbances to wildlife may threaten species that are already vulnerable. Tourism, in particular, may prioritise profit over protection, leading to overcrowding and exploitation of these environments. Furthermore, the high carbon emissions from long-distance travel to such remote destinations contradict the very goal of preserving nature. 

In conclusion, while travelling to remote natural environments carries environmental risks, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages if strict regulations are enforced. Scientific research in these areas is vital for understanding global challenges, and responsible tourism can foster appreciation for nature. However, it is crucial that such activities are carefully controlled to minimise negative impacts.

exam_question: These days, more fathers stay at home and take care of their children while mothers go out to work. What could be the reasons for this? Do you think it is a positive or a negative development?
text:
In today's world, some men tend to choose become a caretaker in the household while women are likely to earn money. This essay will look at some primary causes of this and provide a few my opinions below.

There are several reasons for more fathers to stay at home to take care of their kids while women become the main income in the household. One main cause of this issue is gender equality. To begin with, because of the development of society, some women are aware of their rights and values clearly. To illustrate, for those living in a developing society, they would find job opportunities easier which leads them to earn significant money. As a result, women play as significant a role as men. Another reason that I would like to provide is economic factors. In particular, due to economic pressure, some mothers rush to work to improve their incomes. To illustrate this point, some women having trading ability tend to become their own business, which brings them significant money. Therefore, mothers are more and more likely to be independent about their finances, which makes them tend to go out to work.

In my view, there are several impacts of this trend on society. The first benefit of the more and more fathers who tend to choose becoming a caretaker is that their children will get the attention from both fathers and mothers. For instance, when fathers spend time take care their kids, them will get the protection which help them avoid to potential damage factors from the society such as risk of sexual abuse and risk of being abused. Another advantage of this trend is that some households may balance their finances better. In particular, with basic needs pressure such as food and living cost, fathers and mothers can earn money together to handle such finances problems.

In conclusion, the trend of some men choosing become caretakers in the household while women are likely to earn money seems to be a favorable progress. In my opinion, this tendency has a positive effect.

exam_question: The increase in the production of consumer consumption goods results in damage to the natural environment. What are the causes of this and what can be done to solve this problem?
text:
Nowadats, there has been a dramatic increase in the number of demand and supply. Although many people claim that is is beneficial as it makes our life easier, such approach can lead to the significant environmental damages. Fortunately, being aware of its couses we can find solutions to solve this problem.

Reasons for climate changes resulting in mass consumption are very diversified. First and foremost, they are an effect of the pollution. Greenhouses gases that are send to atmosphere by global corporations as well as toxic wastes throwing away to the see contribute to destruction of natural environment by polluting air and water. Furthermore, deforestation is another cause. In order to built new factories a free space is needed; as a result many trees are cut down to make a room for warehouses and places to work.

However, there have been also ways to prevent envronmental damages. The most significant of them is to rise a global awareness of the problem. If people gain a wider knowledge of our harmful impact on the nature, they will be more sensitive and, therefore, a less damage will be caused. Additionaly, a law should protect environment in a more complex way. The only way to stop climate changes is a cooperation between governments from all over the world, which means a more radical punishment for companies contributing to environmental damege. 

In conclusion, factores such as air and water pollution as well as deforestation have a negative impact on environment. On the other hand, rising awareness of the problem and imposing a penalty for companies responsible for it, is the way to solve the problem.

exam_question: As the number of cars increases, more money has to be spent on road systems. Some people think the government should pay for this. Others, however, think that car users should cover the costs. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
text:
The attitude of today's society has enabled  numerous amount of individuals to have an automobile; as a result, the road infrastructure has enquired enormous investments. Some advocates claim that car owners are responsible for upgrading the system; however, in my opinion, it is the local authorities' liability to cover the expenses.

The feasible reason why drivers should invest their funds on roads is the proliferation of private cars. To be precise, today every tenth resident is eager to possess a vehicle even though there is a lack of its necessity. Undoubtedly, contemporary countries are packed with an ample number of automobiles causing a potential deterioration of the road condition. Indeed, the USA is a prime example of how a car is overused where every resident utilizes it even for shopping goods in a walking distance store. Consequently, it is reasonable to assign the costs to car owners for maintaining and enhancing the infrastructure.

However, in my point of view, people who are in power are the ones who are obliged to provide their citizens with an appropriate transportation system inasmuch as they are already charged an exorbitant amount of tax in order to reside in a well-developed country. To illustrate, people living in Scandinavian countries are forced to part with forty per cent of their income to cover taxation and fairly they anticipate the funds would be allocated on road infrastructure investment. Therefore, if the government considers laying the responsibility for road upgrade works on their town dwellers, it will certainly cause public backlash or outcry as it is inhumane to put the extra financial burden on them.

In summary, although it is quite adequate to deem that car owners are ought to support the road condition, I am highly convinced that the issue concerning road maintenance costs should be covered by the government.

exam_question: some people think the newly built houses should be the same as the old housing styles in local areas. others argue that local authorities should allow people to build houses in their own style. discuss both views and give your opinion.
text:
it is argued whether new buildings should be constructed just the same as the architectural style of the ancient ones or houses should be erected freely as the owners wish to. In my opinion, I totally agree with the second notion and give my own reasons below.

exam_question: Some today argue that schools are no longer necessary because children can learn so much from the internet and be educated at home. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
In this modern era, an abundance of beneficial information can be accessed easily on the internet, among which the educational contents are no exception. A vast variety of different e-books, recordings and videos are available for children to take advantage of as educational sources. 

However, I argue that this could not be totally substituted for conventional schools because there are some shortages associated with it, as well as a lot of irreplaceable characteristics of physical classes.

To commence with, the internet can be used as a rich source of educational files, graphical information, and additional homework for educational purposes. For example, pupils can find documents and photos from alternative sources to supplement their courses and exercise more. Furthermore, the internet eliminates the barrier of location and time by providing these contents for every child regardless of their residence and time zone and as a result, it improves the education of children who live in far-flung areas and developing countries.

On the other hand, some merits are attributed to traditional schools’ lecture halls which can not be rivalled by the internet. For instance, by attending the classes, adolescents become exposed to an opportunity of communication and debate with classmates and teachers which empowers their soft skills. Furthermore, not all internet contents are credible and it needs a degree of expertise to sift information and choose the best to fit their needs. Thus, the need for professional teachers or tutors is still of the essence.

To summarize, although the internet could bring about numerous useful resources for educating children, it can not be completely replaced by schools. It is better to use it as a supplement for studies under the supervision of teachers.

text:

 On the other hand, underdeveloped nations, since they had a chance to see the happenings in their neighbouring state become resilient and content with their economic success will no longer be shaken by its impact. exam_question: Some people think that the best way to increase road safety is to increase the minimum legal age for driving cars and riding motorbikes. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
Unquestionably, highway traffic security plays a crucial role in the transportation system to avoid accidents. A section of the public asserts that to proliferating transport security, the age limit for driving should be increased. Even though escalating the minimum age seems to positive step, I do not agree that is the most effective measure to increase roadway protection.

The maturity factor in driving has been proven to be extremely important in this practice. Thus increasing the minimum age for driving is definitely a step in the right direction. For instance, If youngsters learn driving skills when they are properly mature and handle the traffic congestion, it will not only overcome the risk of incidents but also increases the protection of other people on the roads. This measure, therefore, could prevent youth to use vehicles in cities without appropriate training as well as complete age requirements. However, it is not sufficient to solve the overarching driving concerns.

The difficulty is that age restriction for safe driving is only part of the rules. Research shows that all accidental cases are not only occurred by underage drivers, other various factors are also responsible for these mishappenings such as poor traffic light systems, breakage of road security rules, and does not wear a helmet during driving. Moreover, the government should need to ensure that every individual follows the on-road safety procedures to avoidance of danger. Besides this, people have to realize the importance of equipment such as seatbelts and helmets to prevent road accidents.

To conclude, although age limitation is a step in the right direction, I believe that people have to follow all rules and regulations to ensure transport welfare is the only way to increase protection on roads.

exam_question: Today, many people do not know their neighbors in large citites. What problems does this cause ? What can be done about this ?
text:
Lack of knowledge about surrounding people is considered to be severe in cities. This can cause irritation while living with each other, as well as not getting any help from others, yet this can be solved by organising more social activities for the neighbourhood.

The obvious consequence that not knowing anyone in the neighbourhood is frustration while sharing the living area. It is self-evident that as we are leading an insensitive lifestyle, we will form a self-centered personality, in other words, only live for yourself. When we are selfish in our daily life, we will definetely not know about things that our neighbours want or hate, resulting in doing things that people do not like, causing irritation between individuals. The fact has shown that in Ho Chi Minh City, over 60% of people who are not satisfied with their living conditions all blame for their neighbours do not know their regulations.

In addition, being self-centered, aside from causing frustration for others also make them unable to get any help from the community. Without any relationship with neighbours, the individual will soon be isolated with the neighbourhood since the people around will know nothing about the person unless he or she make some contact with the others. Therefore, it leads to being unsupported in many situations. For example, it will be much harder for a person  with no connection with neighbours to go repair a motorbike than those who have.

Perhaps the simplest solution for the issue is the manager of the residential area have to hold more social activities to bond people. If some person gets outside comfort zone, it shows to this person how exactly this world works. As a result, it will make a future choosing a profession more reasonable. In addition, in such a country as Belarus, only rich people can afford to travel during a gap year, so working is a good choice to get a real experience. Look at me, for instance. I had such an experience. I worked as an assistant of an economist in a small company, and it helped me to get my profession. I studied the economy at university.

	To conclude, despite the fact that I agree with the idea that traveling is a magnificent choice to spend a free year after a graduation, I assume that in some cases a real work can give to young people more experience and ideas.

exam_question: Some people argue that job satisfaction is more important than job security, while others believe that they cannot always expect job satisfaction, and a permanent job is more important. Discuss both these views and give your own opinionSome people argue that job satisfaction is more important than job security, while others believe that they cannot always expect job satisfaction, and a permanent job is more important. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion?
text:
There are controversial perspectives heating a debate over an ideal job.  While some hold a strong view that vocation gratification is of essence, the opposite makes a statement that a stable job is more crucial. Although each has its own perks, I would contend that it is optimal to combine both mentioned facets

Without a shadow of a doubt, employees' complacence plays such a paramount significant role in an ideal occupation. In fact, workers who are content with their line of work conduct their tasks with a higher efficiency and accuracy than those who are not since they are more determined and whole-hearted with their corporation. Google enterprise is an obvious example as they are one of the pioneers who put job contentment as a prerequisite. Workers recruited by Google are provided with top-notch facilities such as air-conditioning systems or game rooms. As a result, they are capable of working with higher accuracy and efficiency as well as relieving their stress if necessary. Indeed, in terms of defining a dream job, being gratified with vocations is of essence

While the redeeming features of gratification are widely acknowledged, it is unfair if those of the long-term commitment of occupation are neglected. In this economy-based world, people desire long-term commitment in their occupations in order to cover their bills and raise their family. Therefore, a number of workers seek a stable line of career instead of a comfortable one. Knowing these facts, many organisations in Japan offer a lucrative range of salary and provide various chances of promotion for workers with high seniority, which prevents them from hopping to another company. It can be seen that apart from job satisfaction, job security is also taken into consideration.

All in all, while it is argued which facet of a job is more vital, both job contentment and stability have their redeeming features, and they should be well combined in order to achieve the term “ideal job”.

exam_question: In some countries, there are fewer young people who listen to or play classical music these days. Why is this? Should young people be encouraged to play or perform classical music?
text:
In the past, the traditional melody was a household name, but nowadays very few youngsters express their interest in learning the traditional melody. In this essay, I will highlight the reason behind this phenomenon and advocate that the younger generation should learn more about traditional melody as there is a myriad of benefits. 

In terms of the causes of the declining interest in traditional melody. One of them is the abundant alternatives available for individuals. As compared to decades ago, youngsters were limited to entertainment like musical instruments, nowadays, they are inundated with numerous entertainment activities such as online gaming and web surfing. Naturally, the traditional melody becomes less popular when its crowd is being drawn towards other recreational activities.

However, I feel that individuals should learn to play classical music. First and foremost, listening to classical music like piano music relaxes individuals’ minds and gives them a hike in productivity. For example, it is scientifically proven that when a student listens to classical music for 15 minutes before he studies, he will enjoy a hike in productivity by 10%. Furthermore, classical music is an essential part of a country’s culture. It is undeniable that the responsibility to pass down traditional culture lies on the shoulders of the younger generation. If they refuse to learn traditional melody, in many years to come, several genres of traditional melody will cease to exist and it is a huge loss for the country. 

In conclusion, the innumerable entertainment choices available for the youth is the primary reason why classical music becomes less popular. However, I concur that youngsters ought to play traditional music, not only does it help to boost their efficiency, but it is also their responsibility to preserve their culture.

exam_question: Some think that climate change reforms will negatively affect business. Others feel they are an opportunity for businesses. Discuss both sides and give your own opinion
text:

exam_question: Many researchers believe that we can now study the behaviour of children to see if they will grow up to be criminals, while others disagree. To what extent do you think crime is determined by genetics? Is it possible to stop children from growing up to be criminals?
text:
It has been a point of contention as to whether scientists should be authorised to study a child's progress as an examination of underlying causes for criminality. Although genes have been brought up as one of the likelihoods for them moving towards a criminal attitude, I believe that the role of a family is far more crucial in their future evil tendencies. In addition, regardless of the chief root of atrocity, psychological therapy could be effective in preventing children from growing to become a criminal.

Genetics would be wrongly considered as a root for criminal conduct, especially when a rare case of wrongdoer appeared, whom the environment that they grow up in, is somewhat normal contrary to regular criminals. In the majority of instances, criminals come from violent families, where their experience would later manifest in the form of exerting power and dominance over others. However, sometimes other factors such as social impacts or peer pressure result in the same implications, which will later be misapprehended as the consequence of genetics. Hence, an individual's traits are often the result of numerous factors, which will be misread as genetic's impact on the person's behaviour.

Moreover, psychology has provided a range of treatments in order to prevent children from becoming a felon. Scientists in this field of study can give useful suggestions for the offspring's upbringing to guide them toward raising a law-abiding citizen. For instance, a number of states in the United States have designated supervisors in the schools to monitor the children and report any sign of misdemeanour. This report will later be used to suggest  the targeted kids to a corresponding psychologist so that they can be worked on and eventually, prevent them from forming that negative characteristic.

In conclusion, genetics cannot be an appropriate reason for criminality as there are numerous other factors that can shape our characteristics. Further, Despite the underlying cause for kids to become evil, psychology can assist to prevent a bad habit from developing as soon as being diagnosed early.

exam_question: Many students find it difficult to pay attention at school. What are the reasons for this? What could be done to solve this problem
text:
Attention is an ability which is crucial for students to focus on their studies. Mainly lack of motivation and interest toward the subject are the two reasons why attention deficit happens. However, this problem could be effectively managed by changing teaching methods to a greater extent. 

To begin with, it has been noticed that learners may not be sufficiently motivated to learn the particular subjects. Mostly, they just attend the class because it was included in the curriculum. Similarly, pupils often find the subject is boring since they could not understand why they are taught this topic. For example, while teaching a foreign language, English, the significance of the subject, its global status, and mastering the subject may offer better career prospectus, all these details to be explained before the beginning the lecture. Otherwise, gradually and slowly, students tend to become inattentive in their classroom and hardly gain any knowledge from the section. 

Nevertheless, this scenario would be tackled by adopting new style of pedagogical methods. Firstly, teachers could incorporate the topic into their day to day life. This may create curiosity in the learners’ mind. After which, audio-visual aids could be added to inculcate interest and keep the onlooker focussed throughout the class. Similarly, instead of having a monotonous lecture, scholars must be encouraged to ask question and clarify their doubts. The education must be a two way communication between teachers and pupil and this may improve the span of attention remarkably. 

In conclusion, attention deficit is a common problem that can be seen among students. Lack of interest and motivation are the culprits of this problem. By changing the olden education style may control the hurdle effectively.

exam_question: People these days watch TV, films and other programmes alone rather than with other people. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
text:
In the present day, some personal habits have been changing due to the advance in technology and globalization. Although some people would rather do some activities alone, the consumption of this kind of entertainment such as television, movies and other activities can promote a variety of results. From my point of view, the positive aspects of habits outweigh the negative ones.

One of the main advantages is the freedom and the solo downtime to think in own life. Certainly, depending on the presence of family and friends is pivotal, however, the opportunity to meditate and think over future plans and serious decisions is of paramount importance to the building of personalities. Furthermore, some alone moments are necessary to learn and focus on specific topics. For instance, some international research demonstrates that a part of the population learn with more facility when they are alone since they need to force their brain to think in a variety of options and speculations. 

Another benefit is related to chances to do activities without interruption resulting in saving time since people do not need to stop to explain some ideas, in other words, the flow of the activity is continuous and more productive. Moreover, when people have an opportunity to do activities without another person close to them, they can put their personal features in each detail, and also perform a duty in their own way. For example, researchers claim that individuals who are more solo present more flourished creativity. Self-awareness and self-knowledge are necessary for the development of human beings. 

There are, however, some disadvantages. The excess of time without family or friends to share daily routines can promote  intense loneliness due to the scarcity of companionship. In addition, the lack of someone to talk to can result in an individual with more likelihood of being diagnosed with mental disorders. Take the current day as an example, because of the coronavirus pandemic, the number of individuals without the presence of parents or some friends increases in high proportion resulting in a variety of diseases such as depression and anxiety. 

In conclusion, spending leisure time alone is essential to understanding a variety of thoughts that leads to wise decisions. Besides that, enjoying our own companionship is a process of self-knowledge. Therefore, the practice of daily habits alone is a great option to grow up.

exam_question: It is now possible for scientists and tourists to travel to remote natural environments, such as the South Pole. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
text:
With the advancement of technology, scientists and tourists can embark on a journey to remote destinations like the Antarctic. While this progress in travel has provided many opportunities for us, some drawbacks need to be considered. In my opinion, the pros of travelling to isolated environments outweigh the cons.

On the one hand, one of the significant challenges we face is maintaining human life and natural balance. Due to the harsh climate and natural phenomena such as snowstorms and avalanches, visitors may jeopardize their lives by travelling to isolated places. Moreover, mass tourism and human tendencies to litter and destroy flora and fauna are other environmental problems. This approach can disrupt the natural habitat and increase the chance of animal extinction in those remote places.

On the other hand, the proponents believe that travelling to remote natural places can provide research opportunities for scientists and bring pleasure and appreciation of untouched nature for many tourists. Studying unknown areas may lead to discoveries that can be the solution to our everyday problems. For example, understanding how animals or plants survive in this wild weather is one of the reasons that humans should pursue. Furthermore, providing opportunities for people to appreciate and enjoy these unique places on Earth is a once-in-a-lifetime experience in every person’s life.

In conclusion, it seems that not only the general public can enjoy unique scenery, but scholars and researchers have the opportunity to solve many human challenges by studying these remote natural environments. In my opinion, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages, and having regulations for monitoring and directing tourists can mitigate the inherent dangers that might happen.

exam_question: The increase in the production of consumer goods results in damage to the natural environment. What are the causes of this? What can be done solve this problem?
text:
Consumer goods have become an indispensable part of modern life, but their production has resulted in significant damages to the environment. This essay discusses why I feel this is happening and explores the measures that can be taken. 

There are several reasons that I believe can be attributed to consumption placing undue stress on the environment. The primary reason is pollution generated during the production process of consumer goods, resulting in the production of large amounts of waste, such as wastewater, plastic materials and electronic waste. The production of electronic products, for example, requires massive production of chemicals, which are non-biodegradable and can lead to soil erosion. The second reason is the depletion of natural resources. For instance, the production of wooden furniture requires logging many trees, leading to deforestation and loss of vital habitats for wildlife. 

There are several measures can be taken to remedy this challenging issue. One effective approach is for companies to use sustainable materials in the production processes. For instance, Starbucks have already replaced plastic straw with the degradable and recycled materials made of paper. Furthermore, governments can introduce regulations which limit the amount of waste discharged during the procession. For example, some greenhouse tax can be imposed local industrials to reduce the amonut of gas emissions. By taking these steps, we can work towards an eco-friendly future. 

In conclusion, more consumption goods has caused environmental damage due to the pollution produced and over usage in natural resources. However, by using sustainable materials and regulating business to encourage more environmental friendly practices, this can be reduced to a manageable level.

exam_question: As the number of cars increases, more money has to be spent on road systems. Some people think the government should pay for this. Others, however, think that the drivers should cover the costs. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
text:
Nowadays, road systems have become more and more important in the modern world due to the increasing number of cars. Some people think that government should take responsibility for the road system, however other people think that drivers should pay for the cost.  My view is that government should pay for the road systems and the drivers should pay for the maintenance.

On the one hand, it is obvious that only the official department has enough money to build a road system all over the country. This is because the government get taxes from citizens and some other business and the government has the right to use taxes to build roads for the country. Moreover, Only the government has resources to build a good transport network around the country. For example, the government can do full research and plan better road systems for the next 100 years, which is impossible for individuals. Therefore, from my point of view, the government should pay for the rest of the road systems.

On the other hand, drivers have no responsibility to cover the costs. Drivers already pay a lot of different taxes before they used the road. For instance, drivers need to pay a transfer fee when they build a car and an oil tax when they fill in petrol. So drivers should not spend anything on building a new road. However, I believe that the government has the right to ask drivers to pay for some parts of the highway due to maintenance fees.

In conclusion, governments need to make sure that money has been used correctly to build a good transport network for citizens.

exam_question: Many people put their personal information online (address, telephone number, and so on) for purposes such as signing up for social networks or online banking. Is this a positive or negative development?
text:

exam_question: Living in a country where you have to speak a foreign language can cause serious social problems, as well as practical problem. To what extend do you agree or disagree with this statement?
text:
There are various inevitable challenges faced by foreigners residing in a different country. One of the issues is the language barrier that induces detrimental effects on the expatriates living abroad. I totally agree with this statement because language barriers can cause social isolation and potential risks in emergency situations.

First and foremost, not being able to converse in the local language may cause social problems as well as a deep sense of isolation. It is simply because native speakers perhaps look down on foreigners when they try to articulate their thought in their accent. After repeated multiple awkward social interactions with the same unwelcoming pattern, they come to a conclusion in which they feel incompetent, insecure and even undesired. For example, the Egyptian Gazette reports that in some countries, such as America, the Egyptian population suffers from a high rate of social isolation due to to development of avoidant social behaviours.

Secondly, having language barriers also may cause potential risks and dangers effects when they face emergency cases. For instance, when Chinese people living in French-speaking countries go to the hospital for any kind of emergency, they might not be able to convey the exact health problem in the right terms or any allergies the patient is having. Moreover, this situation poses a danger to the life of the patient and medical practitioners might miss out important health details about the patient because of the miscommunication. 

In conclusion, I totally agree that the language barrier has a challenging impact on any foreigner’s social and practical life. However, these serious issues can be overcome with the government’s support by providing free language classes in order for the foreign residents to fit in with the local people.

exam_question: Some people believe that it is good to share a much information as possible in scientific research, business and the academic world. Other believe that some information is too important or too valuablr to be shared freely.
text:
It is a common belief that it brings positive effects when people share as much information as possible in scientific research, business and the academic world. However, I firmly believe that some information should be kept a secret since it can be too important or valuable to be shared freely. In the following paragraphs, I will briefly explain my view on this topic.

Every company has its weakness and strength. On the one hand, it is true that technology can improve faster when companies share information and work together. By working together, the companies will develop faster compared to working on their own. For example, in the electric car market, three different companies held hands together working on an electric car by working on different types of parts. As a result, the work efficiency increased considerably by 60 per cent. This shows that when companies share information or work together, it can bring efficiency.

Nevertheless, some information is too important to be shared because it can create a competitor. Information can be technology, and it is precious when it is hidden. However, if other companies have that information, it will be no longer be unique. One clear example is that the company ‘apple’ company lost approximately 70 per cent of its profit when important information got leaked. This is because a competitor company developed this technology as well, and it became a typical technology when it was apple’s technology.

To sum up, while it is apparent that a business can expand faster by sharing information, it is undeniable that keeping the information on its own is more important.

exam_question: Weddings are getting bigger and more expensive. What is the reason for this? Is it a negative or positive development?
text:
Without any qualms, it has become very costly to hold marriages as bigger events. The major causes of this trend are maintenance of social status and expression of uniqueness in the wedding by the individuals. This essay believes that it is a positive progress as it is a sole opportunity of social interaction and strengthening of societal bonds and this ceremony serves as an unforgettable day which brings everyone together and closer.

The primary reason why weddings are becoming lavish and exorbitant is that people aspire to maintain their status in the society and show the wealth to others. To be more precise, spending lots of money to organise marriage function is the symbol of prosperity in the community. Furthermore,  luxurious ceremonies represent uniqueness and bring the couple and their family into limelight. Receiving praise from attendees of the events make them feel contented about arrangements. Also, in recent times, couples try to design and plan their wedding as per their desire which often results in higher expenditure.

In my opinion, this practice is a positive development as wedding day is the only day where one can interact with all the relatives and acquaintances in a company. Strengthening of social bonds is ensured as all the known people are invited to the functions. Huge amount of money is spent in order to honour everyone and represent a reputed status in the society. Moreover, sense of community and togetherness is expressed as such events bring everyone together to celebrate the happy time with the family which makes it an unforgettable day. Matrimonial ceremonies are very special due to which family expenses money as reflection of how precious is this day to them.

In conclusion, maintaining societal status and expressing unique identity at the causes of this tendency. I believe that it is a positive development as it enhances the interaction and strengthen bonds among people and instills sense of community and togetherness.

exam_question: Some believe that the Olympic games help bring people from different nations together, while others claim that holding the Olympics wastes money which could be used for important issues.
text:
Some people may argue that organizing the Olympics may be a waste of money, which is controversial to bridge the gap between nations. From this author’s perspective, the waste of money can be meaningless when compared to the benefit of being closer to different countries.

Firstly, there is an undeniable point that the Olympic games could bring some economic disadvantages for the country organizing due to the exorbitant building in the events. Obviously, because of the expensive amenities for the events such as the conditional sports venue or the equipment for athletes, the host country needs to spend over a billion dollars. Moreover, some sports avenues may need to be more useful when the Olympic games finished due to the characteristic features of sports. For instance, during the Brazil Olympic Games in 2016, the authority spent over 12,2 billion dollars which was enormous even governments asking support from UNCDF. However, there are more benefits to the country when governments can take advantage of being closer to national people like having an increase in income from tourism or creating a good reputation for future foreign investment.

However, the Olympic games can be an advantageous opportunity for collaboration for countries around the world. When athletes join in the most popular international event, they have a chance to interact with other people to explore their skills or culture. Furthermore, some talented athletes can have the opportunity of being invited by some famous clubs which can provide them with a lot of foundation to develop their career. For example, Cristiana Ronaldo was invited to compete for Al  Nassr, which provided him with twice his salary than his former salary.

In conclusion, although the Olympic games can have a negative effect on the economy of the host country, they can help bridge the gap between nations for athletes which brings people a lot of benefits for the future.

exam_question: Today different types of robots are being developed which can serve as companions and workers to help at work and at home. Is this a positive or negative development?
text:
Robots are definitely one of the greatest technological innovations of this world. They are now being used massively at work as well as for domestic purposes. While robots are largely beneficial in saving time and automating  tasks, they have some drawbacks too.

To begin with, they are a good substitute in places where the intervention of humans is dangerous and sometimes impossible. To exemplify, these days robots are widely used in the construction and automobile industry to lift heavy machines and also to assemble certain parts together. Apart from using robots in industries that involve high risk, they are other robots that are also being used in medical, agricultural and other industries. With robots, tasks can be completed easily in less time as well as with minimal errors, thus increasing  productivity. In addition, humans usually get exhausted from doing boring and repetitive tasks; employing robots for such tasks is a sensible idea as the standard of work does not get slammed for the reason that the robots are devices that never-tiring.Last but not the least, in recent years, few individuals started using robots for domestic purposes as well. In some developed countries like America,  few business magnets with extremely busy schedules are purchasing robots to finish most of their works thus replacing home helpers.

While, there are a lot of advantages, there are some drawbacks too. Robots are very expensive and difficult to maintain. They are capable of doing only certain works that they are programmed for. It is not ideal to rely on them at all times as there are many risks associated with them especially with children around. Moreover, using robots can mean lesser employment opportunities. If most of the workforce is replaced by robots, the public will have to depend majorly only on industries related to robots to sustain themselves. There is also a higher risk of hackers invading the robotic software which could turn out to be deadly for the entire world.  On top of that, over-dependence on machines can make people lazy and cause drastic effects on health. 

To conclude, though robots are a positive development in technology, too much dependency on them can cause detrimental impacts on an individual as well as society.  Rather than using robots for every other work at home and in offices, their use must be restricted for specific purposes only where human intervention could be dangerous.

exam_question: The manufacturing and use of cars damages the environment but their popularity is increasing. Why is this? How could this be controlled?
text:
Even though both production and car use increase pollution, the auto industry continues to expand. This is because developing nations now have greater disposable income and governments can limit the resultant environmental damage through regulation.

The main cause underlying an increasing number of cars is growth in developing countries. Ownership in developing countries peaked decades ago and many European nations in particular are now adopting greener modes of transport. However, in developing nations, cars are seen as a status symbol that boost self-esteem and serve a practical travel purpose. Coupled with increased per capita GDP, the boom in car ownership is unsurprising. For example, a growing middle class in Vietnam was driving up purchases of foreign automobiles dramatically over the last decade. The demand is so great that last year a Vietnamese company introduced the first domestically produced car. This same trend is replicated around the world in developing countries.

The most impactful response is from the government. Consumers will continue to buy cars but the government has control over a range of possible environmental protective measures. For example, there could be stricter laws related to emission standards. This would cut down on the average amount of pollution from individual cars and collectively make a huge difference. Another measure would be to discourage car ownership by taxing cars heavily and improving the quality of public transportation. A good example of this would also be in Vietnam where there is a 200% tax on cars and the government is building the world’s most expensive subway system in Ho Chi Minh City. Individuals are unlikely to change their behaviour in mass, so it falls to policy makers to dissuade citizens through proactive reforms and policies.

In conclusion, more cars can be explained by rising incomes globally and pragmatic solutions come from government regulation. If taken seriously, the heavy environmental toll of cars can be curbed.
